In other corporate news, the AI capex hangover continues to spread: Micron paused work on a $4.5 billion Taiwan chip plant after a labor row, and China blocked the roughly $5.4 billion sale of ABB's robotics unit to SoftBank. Meanwhile the hyperscalers that "won" the election are busy raising cash anyway: Meta raised €9 billion in its first euro bond on a record €53 billion of orders, and Microsoft raised $25 billion in a 10-tranche bond offering. Goldman and Apollo are in talks with investors to start selling portions of a roughly $40 billion chip financing deal for SpaceX, and Apple is cutting employee budgets for AI usage as part of a cost-cutting effort. Wendy's rejected a takeover proposal from a Trian Partners-led group; DTE Energy agreed to sell its DTE Vantage business for about $3 billion; SS&C priced an upsized $1.05 billion of convertible notes.

The global framing is unchanged from yesterday: the midterm-fueled rotation out of the AI trade is entering a second day, with previously unloved markets and economically sensitive stocks outperforming at the expense of chipmakers. Asia took the semi pain overnight, with the Kospi tumbling almost 6% (and triggering a trading halt) as SK Hynix and Samsung slumped, while Hong Kong was the other side of the trade, with the Hang Seng Tech index up more than 5%. Europe, the market with the least AI in it, extended its outperformance with the Stoxx 600 surpassing its August closing record.

“Chip names are under pressure because traders see Democrats as bad news for data centers and thus demand for compute,” said Hao Hong, chief investment officer at Lotus Asset Management. “Some money is rotating into consumer names in Korea, China and elsewhere now.”

As Bloomberg's Jan-Patrick Barnert notes, Wednesday's post-vote bounce was fairly ordinary by historical standards: the Dow jumped 3%, the S&P rose 1.6% and the Nasdaq 100 closed up just 0.9% after rising as much as 2.3%, while semis fell 3.1%, energy lost 4.8% and a Goldman basket of AI data-center names sank 5.4% on a day consumer discretionary stocks gained 6.1% (as we noted yesterday). In other words, a typical bounce in a market that is still rotating, rather than healing.

The options market tells the same story: every broad volatility gauge fell (the VIX by 4.2 points to 16.6), but single-stock volatility eased far less and the Cboe dispersion index did not budge, while implied correlation dropped almost 7 points to below 10. That is what a rotation looks like in the options market.

Bloomberg macro strategist Simon White adds that semis are the sector most exposed to a liquidity-driven flattening of the yield curve, with the 3m-10y curve having flattened over 40 bps since early October, at a time when the sector is still crowded despite nursing a drawdown of 30%. "Post midterm fears of data-centre approvals are the sort of trigger that could cajole the crowd to the exits, just as the yield curve flattening exerts extra pressure," he writes.

Over at JPMorgan, Andrew Tyler's Market Intelligence desk says futures point to a continued rotation / Momentum unwind, with "Semis and Memory sell off" continuing, Mag 7 names mixed and defensives leading ex-AI cyclicals premarket. Equity derivatives specialist Christina Jones cautions that the move "feels more positioning-driven versus a true fundamental rotation", adding that "Conviction is low across the board." JPM positioning strategist Arun Jain notes the post-hyperscaler selloff was the second -6z move in Momentum in a week and the largest single-month underperformance in more than 40 years at -5.8z. Tyler remains Tactically Bullish and expects a Tech rebound, arguing that the Blue Wave "has created another wrinkle" for those waiting to re-risk into AI, and that "it tough to see the bottom ahead of capital markets events occurring, though the setup is increasingly attractive."

JPM's credit research team, looking at the data center fallout, says the market will now pay a premium for capacity that is already built: "we used to pay a premium for IG leases, now we are going to pay a premium for stuff that is already built". They don't expect material changes to 2027 capital plans, but see some impact in 2028 and beyond, flagging Texas (about 27% of the MW of data center capacity funded in the HY project finance market) as the primary focus, and expect weakness in IPPs such as VST, TLN and CEG.

Goldman's desks are saying much the same. Rich Privorotsky writes that "The market bought the election dip… thank heaven for everything that wasn't semi-related", and that "This is rotation, not wholesale liquidation." John Flood's "standout theme on our trading desk right now is buying Hyperscalers vs Selling Semis", while Ismail Abbas sums it up: the "new political backdrop is good for those who own compute (hyperscalers) and bad for those who have to build out, sell into, or power datacenters (neoclouds, semis, power, etc)". GS political economist Alec Phillips expects Democratic state and local wins to bring short-term moratoria on data centres, though "these moratoria will not be long-lived" (more in our note from last night). Flood also points out that since 1952 the S&P has averaged +7.5% through year end after midterms and was higher 6 and 12 months later in all 18 cases.

On the macro side, the collapse in the Iran war risk premium remains the other big story: Brent is down about $18 over the last five days (one of its biggest 5-day declines in recent history per Goldman) after Vice President Vance said "The reason we lost is the war" and Trump said it was "largely true" that Republicans lost because of the war, as we discussed yesterday. Lower oil means lower inflation expectations: the 1yr US inflation swap fell to a two-month low of 2.16% on Wednesday, per DB. In Europe, France braces for a day of strikes and demonstrations over the cost of living as budget talks remain deadlocked, while it sells €12 billion of long-dated bonds in a test of demand.

In Europe, the Stoxx 600 rises 0.5% to 660.5 and hit a fresh record, surpassing its August closing high, as the region extends its outperformance driven by the rotation out of the global AI trade and a strong earnings season. Miners are the best performers while telecoms and defense fall as Rheinmetall and Deutsche Telekom results disappoint; Rheinmetall plunged as much as 18% after cutting its sales outlook, extending the post-midterm defense rout. JPM's desk notes Resources, Construction, Banks and Retail are among the top sectors with Telecom and Staples sold, and Beta and Momentum leading. Here are the biggest European movers:

Asian stocks were split down the middle by the rotation. DB's Jim Reid concludes the overnight wrap

In virtually every US election, there is usually some reason why markets are concerned going into it, which then magically fades afterwards. The 2026 midterms seem no different, as yesterday the S&P 500 (+1.58%) posted its best day in three months, whilst bond yields fell sharply around the world. This was mainly driven by relief that the political uncertainty was over, but we also saw concerns ease across the whole range of risk factors that have dominated recent weeks. For instance, Brent crude oil prices (-8.67%) closed beneath $100/bbl for the first time since September, significantly dampening fears over inflation. Similarly, the Franco-German 10yr spread (-11.8bps) tightened sharply, which led to a bit more optimism on Europe. And we even saw a decent rebound in tech stocks, with the NASDAQ (+1.44%) recovering despite fears 24 hours earlier that tech might see a fresh slump.

However as we'll see below some parts of the tech space traded poorly yesterday amid uncertainty as to what the election result will mean for regulation of things such as data centers. This uncertainty has accelerated overnight with Nasdaq futures back down -1.18% and the KOSPI -5.68% lower dragged down by SK hynix (-9.60%) and Samsung (-7.57%). The Korean index triggered a 5 minute trading halt just before I finished typing this.

Elsewhere in Asia, the Nikkei (-1.24%) is also under pressure, as chipmakers and AI-related stocks extended the previous session's declines. In contrast, Chinese equities are outperforming the region in what is developing into a big global rotation over the last 24 hours. The Hang Seng (+3.09%) is benefiting, after also being helped by Beijing unveiling fresh support measures that boosted sentiment toward domestic semiconductor companies. Meanwhile, Australia's S&P/ASX 200 (+2.61%) is also trading significantly higher. S&P 500 futures are down -0.28% so holding on to most of yesterday's gains so far with Stoxx futures (+0.11%) just about maintaining its big boost from yesterday.

This has capped off a remarkable 24 hours for financial markets, with huge moves as investors reacted to the midterm elections. Just to bring you up to speed, it was apparent pretty soon after the counting began that the Democrats were on course to control both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the new Congress, with stronger-than-expected margins in both. Indeed, we’ve already started to see the political consequences, with widespread reports that Republican House Speaker Mike Johnson will step down from leading the House Republicans next year. Meanwhile, CBS reported that Trump had asked advisers if Defense Secretary Hegseth should go. He has been at the hawkish end on the war with Iran, and much of the rally yesterday was linked to a reappraisal of the likelihood of imminent strikes on Iran in light of the election result.

When it came to the market reaction, there was relief among investors that the results weren’t disputed, which helped to reduce political uncertainty. Moreover, the prospect of divided government also eased concerns about the fiscal trajectory, given it’ll now be more difficult to pass tax cuts or spending packages. That helped to bring down Treasury yields, which in turn offered further support to risk assets. In terms of the outcome, it was already expected in polls and prediction markets that the Democrats would win at least one chamber, whilst it was always known that Trump would retain his veto power as well. We did also see a narrative emerge that the scale of the Democratic Party’s win would reduce the leverage of its leftist wing over policy. But when it comes to the headline result, it’s not too different from investor expectations beforehand, even if the scale of the Democratic victory was bigger than expected. In many respects, the overall rally fits into the classic midterm pattern we’ve previously highlighted. After all, in 20 out of 20 midterm elections since WWII, the S&P 500 has been higher one year later. And as I pointed out in my CoTD yesterday, the Republican losses in the House were basically on the historical trendline for what would be expected given President Trump’s approval rating. So it was a very normal election with a very normal market reaction before and after the vote, despite fears that this time would be different.

Nevertheless, there were several equity segments where we did see a specific midterm reaction. For example, Trump Media & Technology Group (-24.54%) had its worst daily performance since 2024. Moreover, some of the most AI-exposed stocks struggled, with CoreWeave (-9.90%) and the Philly semiconductor index (-3.13%) also losing ground. Another underperformer was defence stocks, with the Aerospace & Defense subcomponent of the S&P 500 down -1.25%. But while chips stocks struggled, the Mag-7 (+2.24%) outperformed, led by outsized gains for Microsoft (+6.68%), Amazon (+6.12%) and Apple (+5.31%), with the latter reaching a new all-time high. So sizeable differentiation playing out in the tech space.

The general optimism helped the S&P 500 (+1.58%) to its best day since August, with the gains led by the more cyclical sectors. And the moves received a further boost from another batch of strong US data. For instance, the ADP report on private payrolls showed a +86k increase in October (vs. +67k expected), which added to the optimism before tomorrow’s jobs report. Meanwhile, the ISM services index also came in broadly around consensus at 54.5 in October (vs. 54.8 expected), though encouragingly its prices paid index saw an unexpected decline (73.0 vs 74.0 prev, 74.6 exp.).

Otherwise, markets also got a tailwind from another sharp decline in oil prices, with Brent crude (-8.67%) plummeting again to $94.62/bl. That helped to ease concerns about inflation and saw investors dial back the chance of rapid rate hikes. In part, that followed comments from Vice President JD Vance on X that “The reason we lost is the war”, which implicitly pointed away from a further escalation. And in turn, that led to a huge decline in inflation expectations, with the Euro 1yr inflation swap (-25.9bps) down to a two-month low of 3.10%, whilst the 1yr US inflation swap (-24.9bps) hit a two-month low of 2.16%.

That backdrop led to a big rally for sovereign bonds on both sides of the Atlantic. Treasury yields fell across the curve, with the 2yr yield (-4.9bps) down to 4.58%, whilst the 10yr yield (-7.6bps) fell to 4.89%. They are another -4.3bps lower this morning. And in Europe there were even sharper moves given the continent’s exposure to energy prices. Yields on 10yr bunds (-5.8bps) fell to 3.27%, whilst 10yr OATs (-17.6bps) saw their biggest daily decline since April, falling to 4.77%. That also pushed the Franco-German 10yr spread down by -11.8bps to 150bps, marking its tightest level in the last couple of weeks. And it wasn’t just European bonds that outperformed, as European equities also put in a very strong day. In fact, the STOXX 600 (+1.82%) had its best day since June and the DAX (+2.22%) had its best day since April. European banks (+4.62%) also had their best day since April. So crudely a big rotation from data centres to everything else across the globe.

Looking forward, one of the main highlights today will be the Bank of England’s latest decision at 12:00 London time. They’re widely expected to deliver their first rate hike since 2023, with a 25bp move that takes their policy rate up to 4%. In their preview, our UK economists expect there to be a 6-3 vote tally in favour of a hike, and they think the big changes will come in the form of the BoE’s updated forecasts. Their view is that the Bank will show peak CPI nearer 4.25% in Q1 2027, although they also expect an upgrade to the 2026 growth forecast to 1.4%. For more information, see their full preview here.

There wasn’t much other data yesterday, although we did get the Euro Area flash CPI print for October. That came in as expected by the consensus, with headline inflation up to a 3-year high of +4.0% in October, whilst core inflation remained at +2.5%. Otherwise, the US trade deficit was a bit smaller than expected in September, at $105bn (vs. $107.9bn expected).

Earlier this morning, data showed Australia's seasonally adjusted trade surplus surged to A$2.83bn in September from A$184mn in August, comfortably exceeding economists' expectations of A$940mn and marking the highest surplus in seven months.

In central bank news, minutes from the BOJ's September meeting reinforced the case for further policy tightening. Policymakers generally agreed that interest rates should continue to rise, with one member highlighting the possibility of a faster pace of hikes. Another noted that while there was no need for immediate action, the BOJ should continue to calibrate policy carefully to prevent excessive and persistent inflationary pressures.

Looking at the day ahead, we’ll get the Bank of England’s latest policy decision, and hear from ECB President Lagarde, the ECB’s Cipollone, Moulin, Schnabel, Zigman, Lane, Nagel and Dolenc, and the Fed’s Hammack and Barkin. Otherwise, data releases from Europe include German factory orders and Euro Area PPI for September, along with the October construction PMIs from Germany and the UK. In the US, we’ll also get the weekly initial jobless claims, and nonfarm productivity for Q3.

items.title: Brent On Track For Worst Week Since COVID, But UBS Warns Bears: "Fundamentals Still Provide A Floor"
items.content_text:
Brent On Track For Worst Week Since COVID, But UBS Warns Bears: "Fundamentals Still Provide A Floor"

Brent crude futures are on track for their largest weekly decline since the week ending April 24, 2020, during the early COVID-19 pandemic era, on the prospect that a Democratic sweep could end the US-Iran conflict.

UBS energy expert Dominic Ellis wrote in a note earlier that the collapse in crude's war risk premium reflects the prospects for peace and the potential for the Strait of Hormuz to fully reopen. But those hopes are colliding with the harsh reality that replenishing depleted global oil stockpiles could take considerable time.

Brent's $20 plunge over the last several days reflects a massive unwinding of the war risk premium rather than a meaningful improvement in supply and demand, Ellis said. He estimates that another $10 to $15 of premium remains embedded in crude near $95, leaving more room for downside if further diplomatic signals emerge from the Gulf.

Ellis explained:

The more than $20 decline in Brent over the last week reflects bearish sentiment and a rapid unwind of the geopolitical risk premium in the price rather than a change in supply/demand fundamentals. I'd guess there is still $10-15 of risk premium reflected in the current $95 level, and while there is risk of an ongoing unwind if the Iran-US narrative continues to trend towards de-escalation, it is worth reflecting on what has really changed.

Senior figures in the Republican party, including vice president Vance, are openly acknowledging the role that the Middle East conflict played in the Blue sweep on Tuesday, and even President Trump has admitted that the war may have had an impact on the outcome of the elections. 

But while Trump has recently downplayed the potential for new strikes on Iran, it isn't yet clear the US is ready either to make the major concessions likely needed to move the diplomatic process forward or to declare "job done" and walk away from the conflict, essentially leaving Iran with a Pyrrhic victory but a victory nonetheless. It is hard to have conviction in opaque political process, but it is clear that the market has over the last 7 months been too eager to price in de-escalation ahead of supporting evidence, and I fear the same thing may be happening now.

However, Ellis pointed out that the conflict has drained nearly 700 million barrels from global inventories, as fundamentals still point to a severe global energy crisis that won't dissipate anytime soon.

He said:

Even in the event that I am wrong and this is the dawn of a new era of diplomatic outreach, a new Iran deal and a clear path back towards the normalization of energy exports, the near 700 mn drawdown in global inventories as a result of the conflict so far and the at least 40-50mb ongoing monthly inventory draw if the conflict continues will drive incremental demand that keeps a floor on oil for the next 18-24 months.

The takeaway is that further peace headlines and a possible resolution could push oil prices lower, but the reality is that stockpiles around the world need to be replenished, which should eventually put a floor under prices.

For instance, US distillate stockpiles fell below 100 million barrels for the first time since 2003.

It's great news that US diesel prices hit two-month lows on Wednesday, but traders will have to reckon with depleted inventories (read here).

items.title: Rheinmetall Crashes Most In Months After Guidance Cut (Again) On Military Ramp-Up Risk
items.content_text:
Rheinmetall Crashes Most In Months After Guidance Cut (Again) On Military Ramp-Up Risk

Rheinmetall AG shares plunged the most since late June in European trading after the German defense manufacturer slashed its annual sales forecast for the second time in months. Berenberg analysts pointed out that "Weapon & Ammunition drives most of the guidance cut."

The company, which makes tanks and armored vehicles, artillery, ammunition, air-defense systems and military electronics, now expects 2026 revenue of about $14.8 billion, down from its previous forecast of $15.37 billion to $15.93 billion. The operating margin forecast was also pared down to 18.5% from 19%. A guidance cut in August followed Germany's cancellation of orders for six F126 frigates.

Berenberg defense analyst George McWhirter provided a first-take analysis of the earnings release: em>Weapon & Ammunition drives most of the guidance cut: Rheinmetall's Q3 release this morning provides more detail following the Q3 pre-release and full-year guidance downgrade yesterday evening. Weapon & Ammunition drives most of the cut to the full-year guidance, with the remainder attributed to Vehicle Systems. There is no updated order intake guidance provided. The downgrade highlights the execution and order intake risk, stemming from the significant ramp-up in defence programmes to 2030, which poses a risk to medium-term estimates, in our view. Key details to look out for on the conference call at 1pm UK time (2pm CET) include the company's updated estimate on the timing and size of the Arminius contract award, as well as the company's Q4 order intake expectations. We expect the shares to underperform.

VS and W&A weaker in Q3: Q3 revenue increased by 32% to €3,149m, 3.2% below Vara consensus; the miss was driven by Vehicle Systems (VS) and Weapons & Ammunition (W&A). VS revenue increased 9.6% yoy to €1,467m (5.3% below consensus), and W&A revenue increased 37.3% yoy to €949m (5.1% behind consensus). This weakness was offset by beats in other divisions; Air Defence (AD) revenue grew 64.9% to €254m (6.6% ahead of consensus), Digital Systems (DS) grew 38.7% to €509m (3.1% ahead of consensus) and Naval Systems (NS) revenue of €345m was 13.7% ahead of consensus.

Air Defence drives Q3 EBIT beat: Q3 operating profit increased 53.6% to €553m (4.1% above consensus), equating to a margin of 17.5% (up by 270bp yoy). VS and W&A were weaker again; VS rose 13.7% to €191m (2.4% below consensus), while W&A grew 35.6% to €217m (11.4% below consensus). Basic EPS pre-PPA from continuing operations increased by 62.1% yoy to €6.42, -7.2% below consensus. Operating FCF was -€82m (consensus: €123m), reflecting continued build-up of inventories and investment. Rheinmetall Nomination fell by 25% yoy to €2,893m. The total order backlog, including framework contracts, fell sequentially to €78.0bn versus €80.5bn at H1.

Lowered FY 2026 EBIT guidance 8% below consensus: Full-year guidance was lowered yesterday evening. The revenue guidance was lowered by 5% at the mid-point to €13.2bn (5% below consensus). The majority of the cut stems from W&A (€500m cut at the mid-point). The VS revenue guidance has also been lowered by €100m at the mid-point. The operating margin guidance has also been lowered to 18.5% from 19.0%, implying operating profit of €2,442m (8% below consensus). The driver is a c1ppt cut to the W&A operating profit margin guidance to 28-29%, and guidance for a c12% margin in VS (previously: 12-13%). Positive FCF is still expected for the year (consensus: €2,236m), but the previous guidance of >40% cash conversion has not been reiterated. The updated full-year guidance implies 25% growth yoy in Q4 revenue to c€4,824m, and 5% growth yoy in operating profit to €1,103m, equating to a Q4 operating profit margin of 22.9% (-410bp yoy). The updated FCF guidance implies an inflow of above c€1.7bn in Q4 to reach positive territory, versus c€2,008m in Q4 2025.

The second outlook cut in months briefly triggered a trading halt in Frankfurt. Shares plunged more than 18%, pushing the stock to a 52-week low. Much of the blame for the earnings cut centered on delays in its Boxer armored vehicle program. 

In Europe and the US, defense stocks tracked by Goldman were hammered on Wednesday after the Democratic Party's sweep in the US midterms raised concerns that a rearmament supercycle could be derailed.

According to Bloomberg data, 24 analysts are "Buy" rated on the stock, while 5 hold "Neutral" ratings, and zero sell. 

The Goldman US Defense index has slumped toward 2026 lows amid fears that Democrats will slash the military budget next year. 

... and how will the West meet the massive surge in demand for arms driven by Ukraine and US demands if Democrats are expected to slash budgets?

items.title: 'Digital ID Checks For All': Ofcom's Plan For UK's Under-16 Social Media Ban Puts Adults In The Age-Check Line Too
items.content_text:
'Digital ID Checks For All': Ofcom's Plan For UK's Under-16 Social Media Ban Puts Adults In The Age-Check Line Too

Privacy campaigners have argued for months that this is where an age ban ends up. In March, Big Brother Watch titled a post "A social media ban for under-16s = digital ID checks for all" and argued that because the alternatives are intrusive and unreliable, ID would be required in many millions of cases. "All of the online age verification options are highly invasive and the biometric and behavioural profiling options are highly inaccurate, meaning IDs will be required in many millions of cases regardless," the group wrote.

Britain's communications regulator now points the same way. Ofcom's rapid assessment, published Oct. 29, says the face scans social media platforms use to estimate ages are too imprecise to police the government's coming ban for under-16s on their own, and that a second check, often photo ID, will have to back them up. And the checks won't stop at teenagers: many adults with existing accounts will be asked to prove their age as well.

Ofcom named four methods it considers capable of being highly effective at 16, Digit reported: photo ID matching, banking information, digital identity services and facial age estimation. Photo ID matching compares the photo on a passport or driving licence with a live image of the user. A bank check uses age data the bank holds, with the user's consent. A digital ID service lets a person prove their age once with photo ID and reuse it.

The face scan is the weak link. Ofcom says some of the technologies have a margin of error of a few years at 16, so it wants platforms to take a "challenge age" approach, Advanced Television reported, modeled on the "Challenge 25" rule shops use for alcohol. Anyone the software can't place clearly on the right side of the line gets a second, verified check.

That second check is where documents come in. Ofcom estimates that about 94% of people in the UK aged 16 and over hold a passport or driving licence. Around 150,000 16- and 17-year-olds hold neither, and the regulator says those teenagers would likely need to obtain one. About 90% of 16- and 17-year-olds have a bank account, which Ofcom treats as another route.

Adults are not exempt. A platform that already holds accurate, reliable age data on an existing account may skip the check, but many adults will still be asked to prove their age using the wider set of 18-plus methods in Ofcom's existing guidance. Ofcom ruled out the lighter-touch options - credit-card checks, mobile-network checks, email-based estimation and verifiable parental consent - at 16, Reed Smith noted, and said behavioral age inference can help catch under-16s who slip through but cannot serve as the gate.

Big Brother Watch answered the assessment the day it came out. "This plan for a government 'social media ban' is a national ID system by the back door," the group posted on X, adding that "both the government and Ofcom have admitted that children will get around the ban." "The plan will kill anonymity online," it said, Cybernews reported.

🚨BREAKING: All Britons may need ID to use social media, the UK's online safety regulator today announces

"This plan for a government 'social media ban' is a national ID system by the back door. 

Both the government and Ofcom have admitted that children will get around the ban,... pic.twitter.com/QdweEJdK0n

— Big Brother Watch (@BigBrotherWatch) October 29, 2026

Security researchers warn the documents themselves become the target. "Photo ID matching brings highly sensitive documents and facial images into the process, potentially creating another attractive target for criminals," Pieter Arntz, a senior malware intelligence analyst at Malwarebytes, told TechRadar. "The risks aren't hypothetical: as I reported last year, a breach at a third-party support provider for Discord exposed government ID images belonging to around 70,000 users." His conclusion: "Proving you are old enough should not mean revealing who you are."

Even the UK's data regulator is hedging. Katie Searle, the Information Commissioner's Office director of children's strategy, said age assurance "must be implemented in a way that keeps people's personal information safe and allows them to exercise their information rights."

And for all that, the ban may not keep teenagers off. Ofcom Chief Executive Dame Melanie Dawes said, "This ban will shape the future of children's lives online, so it's important to get it right," but she also said motivated children will seek to bypass the restrictions, comparing the ban to alcohol laws that cannot stop underage drinking completely. Australia's ban took effect Dec. 10, 2025, and the country's eSafety regulator found more than eight in ten Australian teenagers still using social media three months later, Reuters reported in August.

The government's own June announcement did not say what the checks would be, and left that to Ofcom. When it announced the ban on June 15, it named Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook and X among the platforms in scope and promised regulations before Christmas, with restrictions expected in spring 2027. The Technology Secretary's letter to Ofcom that day asked it to consider how checks could avoid excluding users who lack passports or driving licences.

The ID push around the ban has been building. As we reported, the under-16 proposal arrived alongside a wider online ID drive, Apple's iOS 26.4 update already asks UK users to prove they are adults with a credit card or ID scan, and an Epoch Times analysis we ran argued a minors' ban requires data from everyone. Ofcom's assessment is the first official look at what that means in practice: a face scan that may not hold up, then a passport, a bank check or a digital ID - for teenagers and adults alike.

items.title: After Mamdani, Los Angeles Is Next: Socialist Nithya Raman Projected To Oust Karen Bass
items.content_text:
After Mamdani, Los Angeles Is Next: Socialist Nithya Raman Projected To Oust Karen Bass

On a night Democrats swept the midterms, Los Angeles moved further left than anyone in the party establishment wanted. Decision Desk HQ projected Wednesday evening that City Councilmember Nithya Raman, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, has unseated Mayor Karen Bass, which would make her the first socialist elected mayor of the nation's second-largest city.

Decision Desk HQ projects Nithya Raman wins the CA Los Angeles Mayor Nonpartisan General Election#DecisionMade: 7:49 PM EST

Follow live results here: https://t.co/1kpbRZUYUv pic.twitter.com/LHwjhhfjjz

— Decision Desk HQ (@DecisionDeskHQ) November 5, 2026

In the county registrar's Wednesday afternoon update, Raman led 405,193 votes (51.7%) to 379,069 (48.3%), a margin of 26,124, according to NBC Los Angeles. Every update since the polls closed has moved her way. Bass led by about 10,600 votes at 9 p.m. Tuesday; by the 3:11 a.m. count Raman was ahead by 16,594.

It isn't final. The Associated Press has not called the race, and with roughly two-thirds of the expected vote counted, about 842,000 ballots remain to be tallied countywide, most of them by mail. Bass has not conceded; her campaign declined to comment Wednesday. The registrar will post updates daily through Nov. 13, and the county certifies by Nov. 27.

Raman claimed the mood of the night from a stage outside the Greek Theatre on Tuesday. "Today all across America, voters demanded change," she said. "For too long our broken and unjust status quo has convinced Angelenos that this is the best that we can do."

Nithya Raman takes the stage outside the Greek Theatre, saying, "I'm hopeful. I'm very hopeful. But I'm also very superstitious so we're going to stay cool." pic.twitter.com/hXIbNVSD3c

— Louis Keene (@thislouis) November 4, 2026

Bass, at her own party at the Loews Hollywood Hotel, told supporters, "This is the Los Angeles that I will never stop fighting for."

From Ally To Challenger

Raman won her Council District 4 seat in 2020 by unseating incumbent David Ryu. She had endorsed Bass for reelection, then filed to run against her on Feb. 7, hours before the deadline. 

"I love this city so much and I think it needs a fighter," she said at the time, according to Fox News.

Her path to the runoff ran through Spencer Pratt. In the June 2 primary Bass finished first with 34.3%, and Pratt, the Republican former star of The Hills, held second on election night before late ballots pushed Raman past him, as we reported at the time. She finished with 29.0% to his 25.5%.

Her ties to the DSA have not been smooth. Its Los Angeles chapter endorsed her in 2020, censured her in 2024 over her acceptance of an endorsement from Democrats for Israel-LA and disagreements over Gaza, and endorsed her again this cycle. She says she makes her council decisions independently of the group.

A Term Defined By The Fires

Bass ran on the endorsements of Gov. Gavin Newsom, Kamala Harris, Nancy Pelosi and major unions, and all 14 of her council colleagues backed her. She also ran on a record dominated by the January 2025 fires, which broke out while she was on a trip to Africa. "It was a mistake to travel, but I will tell you that we need to evaluate everything," she said during the campaign.

Raman made that the center of her closing argument:

Mayor Bass has shown she is not capable of leading our city through disaster.

In LA's darkest moments, she's been missing in action. Our communities have already paid too high a price for her failures.

Four more years is a risk Los Angeles cannot afford. pic.twitter.com/yK0iWpdVM5

— Nithya Raman (@nithyavraman) October 30, 2026

What Comes Next

Raman has campaigned on building housing faster, cutting homelessness, bringing back entertainment jobs and better city services. She has also said she plans to fire LAPD Chief Jim McDonnell, and the police union is already sounding the alarm.

"If Nithya Raman becomes the mayor, the city needs to prepare for Armageddon," said Jamie McBride, a leader of the LAPD officers' union. "She won't have to defund the police; police officers will just leave the department."

Conservatives weren't waiting for the AP:

Los Angeles just Elected Nithya Raman, a dues-paying member of the Democratic Socialists of America, to be their next Mayor.

Raman oversaw all fraud as the chair of the homelessness committee and despite having a $1 billion budget, homelessness rose. She is directly responsible... pic.twitter.com/JVSc96LysL

— Benny Johnson (@bennyjohnson) November 5, 2026

If the count holds, the two largest cities in America will both be run by members of the Democratic Socialists of America, and Los Angeles will get to find out whether it goes better than it has in Zohran Mamdani's New York.

items.content_text:
Prison Time For Discussing The Great Replacement? French Left-Wing Lawmakers Push For Draconian New Law

Authored by Remix News Staff via Remix News,

In the aftermath of a deadly shooting in Trappes, the left, including the mayor of Trappes, is pushing to criminalize discussions of demographic change, the "Great Replacement" theory, or "remigration." If they succeed, French people and politicians could face up to three years in prison for describing the Great Replacement.

🇫🇷🔴 The French could face prison for mentioning the Great Replacement under a new proposal. The mayor of Trappes, Ali Rabeh, is calling for a change in the law to criminalize those who claim that replacement immigration is occurring against the ethnic French population. Rabeh, who holds dual Moroccan and French citizenship, suggests that the Constitution could even be amended to pass the draconian speech law. On the same day he made this proposal, Green (EELV) parliamentarians, including deputies Sabrina Sebaihi and Steevy Gustave, filed related legislative proposals to strengthen sanctions against those discussing the Great Replacement or remigration. Follow: @RMXnews

— Remix News & Views (@RMXnews) November 3, 2026

Critics, including Reconquête party leader Éric Zemmour and others, call the measures an authoritarian assault on free expression that seeks to ban observation of well-documented population shifts rather than conspiracy theories alone.

The left is trying to capitalize on a shooting from Oct. 23, 2026, in Trappes and nearby La Verrière. Kevin T. killed Pengo Bossio Wangi and wounded seven others, reportedly targeting people of Muslim, African, or North African appearance. He told investigators he could no longer stand being "invaded."

Prison for mentioning the Great Replacement

Mayor Ali Rabeh - of the Génération.s party and who holds dual Moroccan-French citizenship - responded on France Inter by arguing that existing hate-speech rules under the 1881 press law are insufficient. He proposed amending Article 24 to punish those who present groups, "by reason of their origin or belonging to a religion, an ethnicity or a supposed race," as agents of a process of replacement of an "alleged native white French people" by immigration or the descendants of immigration.

Rabeh explicitly linked the shooter's language to the Great Replacement, which was first described by Renaud Camus. He said the National Rally had "ideologically armed" the attacker. He suggested that, if necessary, the Constitution itself should be amended.

The Great Replacement "is not a theory, but the name for a phenomenon that I consider the most important of our time. With this chrononym we can describe our era of the beginning of the 21st century to characterize the century as that of the Great Population Exchange, comparable to the Great War, the Great Depression, and the Great Plague," said French philosopher and author Renaud Camus.

The same day, Green deputies Sabrina Sebaihi and Steevy Gustave deposited a bill in the National Assembly, and a parallel text was filed in the Senate by Akli Mellouli. The proposals would specify that provocation to discrimination, hatred, or violence can arise from remarks invoking "the replacement of one population by another or the necessity of a remigration" when they designate a group as a threat because of origin or real or supposed ethnic or national belonging.

Penalties would be aggravated for elected officials or candidates, resulting in up to three years' imprisonment and a €75,000 fine.

Sebaihi framed the move on X:

Les mots tuent. À Trappes, ils ont tué. Avec Akli Mellouli et Steevy Gustave, nous déposons une proposition de loi contre les discours de haine raciste. « Grand remplacement », « remigration » : ce ne sont pas des opinions, ce sont des munitions. Leurs promoteurs doivent en répondre devant la loi.

— Sabrina Sebaihi (@SabrinaSebaihi) October 30, 2026

The reaction from the right was pointed, with Éric Zemmour writing:

Le goulag est en marche. Voilà le projet de leur République socialo-islamique.

— Eric Zemmour (@ZemmourEric) October 30, 2026

Other voices argued the proposals criminalize demographic reality rather than a supposed "conspiracy." Commentators noted that INSEE data show substantial foreign-national and immigrant shares in Trappes, at approximately 30 percent. However, the proportion of ethnic French is far lower than the data suggests, with INSEE refusing to publish statistics on second-generation migrants with French citizenship. In reality, most reports indicate that ethnic French are very much in the minority in the city.

Constitutionalists such as Benjamin Morel and Anne-Charlène Bezzina warned that the texts risk a disproportionate restriction on free expression, that existing incitement-to-hatred provisions already cover clear cases. Morel also writes that the Constitutional Council or European Court of Human Rights would likely strike down such a measure due to freedom of speech in Europe.

Camus says the Great Replacement is "not a theory"

Renaud Camus, the writer who coined the phrase, has continued to insist the underlying phenomenon is real and observable, distinguishing it from unfounded conspiracy claims.

In an interview released last week in the German newspaper Welt, he stated that the Great Replacement "is not a theory, but the name for a phenomenon that I consider the most important of our time. With this chrononym we can describe our era of the beginning of the 21st century to characterize the century as that of the Great Population Exchange, comparable to the Great War, the Great Depression, and the Great Plague."

He further stated: "My opponents may reject the term, but they admit the fact. Even Jean-Luc Mélenchon speaks of creolization. Everyone admits that the composition of the population in France has changed."

🇫🇷🚨 French far-left leader calls for the Great Replacement Jean-Luc Mélenchon: "France is destined to be a Creole (mixed Black and French) nation and so much the better! Let the young generation do the replacement of the old... Each generation is a new people!"

— Remix News & Views (@RMXnews) February 7, 2025

Remigration advocates view the legislative push as confirmation that authorities prefer to suppress discussion of the scale and consequences of post-war migration rather than address integration failures, security issues, or public opinion. They point out that the same political forces have, on other occasions, spoken positively of demographic "créolisation" or the "new France."

The Great Replacement is also not merely a "lofty theory" discussed among a niche group of right-wingers, but a mainstream and recognized development by the French public. Polling shows that 60 percent of the French believe the Great Replacement is occurring, which involves the replacement of ethnic French people with people from Africa, Asia, and other countries.

Under such a law, even France's most famed author, Michel Houellebecq, could face prison time if he were to call the Great Replacement a "fact" again, as he did in 2022.

Whether the proposals to criminalize discussions of the Great Replacement actually advance in a fragmented National Assembly remains uncertain. What is clear is that the left is actively preparing such measures, and should they gain power, many citizens, including politicians, could be headed to prison for simply describing a clear and undeniable statistical reality taking place across Europe.

Tyler Durden Thu, 11/05/2026 - 06:00

items.title: 印度金融机构遭黑客利用 AI 工具发动的网络攻击
items.content_text: 印度计算机应急响应小组（CERT-In）星期三发布安全通报，被称为“狡猾猎鹰”（Crafty Falcon）的黑客组织，已入侵非银行贷款机构、金融科技公司及加密货币交易所。攻击者利用公开可用的 AI 工具，实现高速自动化入侵。印度计算机应急响应小组形容这项威胁“仍在发生，且持续活跃”。该机构点名四款用于入侵的工具，分别是 ARTEX、PentAGI、Cairn 和 CyberStrikeAI。ARTEX 此前曾被用于攻击韩国银行。印度计算机应急响应小组没有说明这些攻击事件由谁发动，也未透露该组织的运作地点。该机构也没有称这些攻击由国家支持或主导，且其点名的攻击工具均可在网络上免费获取。

items.title: 同步导致电网呈现周期为一分钟的震荡
items.content_text: 今天的电网接入了数以百万计的数字控制设备，为了维持电力供需平衡，精准预测和实时控制必不可少。电力系统因此转变成为一种信息物理融合的基础设施（Cyber–Physical Infrastructure）。物理设备与数字控制系统之间形成了紧密的相互依存关系，在带来前所未有的效率与灵活性的同时也引入了新的系统性风险。根据发表在《Nature Energy》期刊上的一项研究，德国研究人员指出全球电力系统存在的一种由信息物理同步效应所引发的、周期为一分钟的相干振荡现象。除了故障和恶意攻击外，即使是良性的控制程序，当大量设备以协同一致的方式运行时，也可能产生系统层面的影响。在大规模信息物理能源系统中，非预期的同步行为可能引发反复出现且具有潜在放大效应的振荡现象。

items.title: 越南对足球直播盗版者判刑最高一年
items.content_text: 越南一家法院对 14 名参与盗版足球赛事直播网站 Bun Cha TV 的团队判处最高一年徒刑。4 名内容、编程和运营团队负责人被判处 12 个月徒刑，另外 5 人判处 10 个月监禁，2 人判处 8 个月监禁，3 名解说员被判处 10 个月缓刑。所有 14 名被告都承认了指控，配合了调查。Bun Cha TV 累计直播逾 15 万场体育赛事，通过博彩及赌博广告非法获利逾 200 亿越南盾（约 512 万人民币）。内容团队负责人获利逾 4.3 亿越南盾，解说员非法所得则在 3100 万到 4.8 亿越南盾不等。美国 MPAA 的代表称赞了这一判决。

items.title: 白宫网络监测到住宅代理活动
items.content_text: 安全公司 Layer3 Intel 报告，他们在分配给白宫的自治系统 AS2650 中监测到住宅代理服务的活动。住宅代理服务会将用户的网络地址租给其他人使用。Layer3 在 10 月 5 日-11 月 3 日期间观察到了 236 次住宅代理连接活动。住宅代理的源头被认为来自 Windows 11 设备安装的俄罗斯代理程序 Infatica。Layer3 Intel 指出，在30 天内有 26 天出现了源自白宫的代理出口节点流量，涉及 6 个 IP，大部分活动发生在傍晚，即下午 5 点至午夜之间。

items.title: Bazzite 45 释出
items.content_text: 基于 Fedora 的游戏发行版 Bazzite 释出了 v45。主要变化包括；基于 Fedora 45，更新 Open Gaming Collective(OGC)内核，支持罗技 TrueWheel 设备等等。过去几年 Linux 对游戏的支持有了显著改善，但对很多用户而言仍然需要自行配置。Bazzite 项目旨在让 Linux 桌面用户无需额外配置就能畅玩游戏，设计类似 Valve 的 SteamOS，但更适合通用桌面使用情景：SteamOS 主要支持 AMD GPU，Bazzite 包含了私有的 NVIDIA 驱动。

items.title: Google 和 OpenAI 的模型对特定口音有偏见
items.content_text: 研究人员调查了先进多模态模型如何评估面试、会议报告和英语口语能力测试中的语音，测试的模型包括了 Google 的 Gemini 2.5 Pro 和 Gemini 2.5 Flash，以及 OpenAI 的 GPT-Audio 1.5，开放权重模型 Qwen 3 Omni。这些模型对五种不同口音——美国、英国、中国、印度和尼日利亚——的英语语音进行了评分。AI 模型普遍将中国和尼日利亚口音的评分最低，印度口音居中，美国和英国口音的评分最高。即使内容完全相同，系统仍然认为美国和英国口音的表达方式和内容都更胜一筹。研究团队发现，明显的等级划分也体现在模型的解释中。研究人员说，模型反复声称中国和尼日利亚口音的英语使用者含糊不清或难以理解，但实际上它们非常擅长转录带有口音的语音，它们理解说话者，但它们只是基于口音，对说话者存在一种隐性的等级观念。

items.title: 富钾盐替换普通盐有助于每年预防数百万人死亡
items.content_text: 澳大利亚乔治全球健康研究院的研究人员评估了在 193 个国家将食盐供应转换为富钾盐的健康益处。他们发现，全球每年可预防近 300 万例死亡和 1000 万例心血管疾病和肾脏疾病新发病例。富钾盐是通过用氯化钾替代部分氯化钠（即普通食盐的主要成分）制成的。它在外观、味道和烹饪方式上都与普通食盐一样。2025 年世界卫生组织（WHO）认可使用富钾盐来降低血压和心血管疾病风险。全球范围内，30-79 岁成年人中有三分之一患有高血压，相当于约 14 亿人。心血管疾病（CVD）是全球死亡和残疾的主要原因，2023 年导致 1920 万人死亡，过去 30 年增加了近 50%。虽然潜在益处很大，但一个担忧是晚期肾病患者出现高钾血症（血钾水平过高）的风险。然而，研究发现，即使在晚期肾病患者中，益处也大于风险。

items.title: Swift 天文台从印尼上空重返大气层
items.content_text: NASA Neil Gehrels Swift 天文台于 11 月 4 日 7:39 a.m. EST 从印尼苏门答腊上空再入大气层，坐标为北纬 3.4 度、东经 98.6 度。天文台的大部分组件在重返大气层过程中烧毁，可能有部分组件幸存下来。Swift 天文台重 1.5 吨，于 2004 年发射升空，旨在研究高能伽马射线暴的起源。过去 22 年受大气阻力的影响 Swift 天文台的轨道高度在缓慢下降，过去两年的太阳活动加速了其坠落。今年 7 月 NASA 曾尝试了一次拯救任务，但任务失败。

items.title: 任天堂最大 ROM 芯片供应商准备退出
items.content_text: 任天堂 Switch 游戏机实体游戏卡带使用的 ROM 芯片供应也受到了 AI 热的影响。任天堂最大 ROM 芯片供应商旺宏电子在其第三季度财报中宣布它准备终止 ROM 芯片生产，脱离游戏行业。旺宏电子表示，ROM 芯片的产量在过去一年中缩减了 39%，目前仅占其业务总量的 5%。ROM 芯片正逐渐被利润更高、需求更旺盛的其它存储芯片所取代。这意味着任天堂未来只能依靠其它 ROM 芯片供应商如罗姆（Rohm）和蓝碧半导体（Lapis Semiconductor），意味着游戏卡带生产成本可能会进一步上升。任天堂已经承诺未来会继续提供实体游戏卡带，不会效仿索尼只提供游戏的数字版本。

items.title: 新型牙刷通过产生电对抗牙菌斑病原体
items.content_text: 一款新型牙刷可通过刷毛移动产生电能，进而可对抗产生牙菌斑的病原体。在为期 3 个月、涉及 115 名志愿者的试验中，牙刷在减少口腔中导致龋齿和牙周炎的细菌方面的效果优于常规的机械刷牙法。牙刷是人类对抗牙菌斑的最强战士，它每晚都能物理性地清除牙齿上的细菌生物膜。然而细菌总会卷土重来，因此每天早晨都会重新开始这场战斗。北京大学口腔医学院的研究人员研发出一种牙刷，其压电单丝刷毛在刷牙过程中弯曲时会产生电荷。这一过程会产生活性氧，进而能破坏牙齿上的生物膜。在实验室中，该装置能有效杀灭口腔病原体，如牙龈卟啉单胞菌（Porphyromonas gingivalis，可引发牙周炎）。研究人员还在真实口腔环境中评估了这种牙刷的实用性。他们将这种牙刷分发给总计 115 名志愿者，这些人都接受了相同的刷牙指导。根据对样本的基因测序和宏基因组测序结果，志愿者口腔中有几种口腔病原体的相对丰度有所下降。总体而言，与传统尼龙刷毛牙刷相比，这种牙刷能更好地控制牙菌斑、减轻牙龈炎症和出血。

items.title: AMD 营收预计将首次超过英特尔
items.content_text: AMD 周二公布了 2026 财年第三季度财报，营收同比增长 45% 达到 134 亿美元。其中数据中心业务贡献了 85 亿美元营收同比增长 97%。客户端与游戏业务部门的营收下滑了 8% 降至 37 亿美元。作为 AMD 在 x86 市场的主要竞争对手，英特尔下一季度营收预计为 150-160 亿美元，其增长几乎停滞。相比下 AMD 预计下一季度营收将达到约 170 亿美元。如果达到这一目标，这将标志着 AMD 营收首次超过英特尔。

items.title: 韩国游戏 PC 启动器被植入恶意代码
items.content_text: 韩国游戏《胜利女神：新的希望（NIKKE）》的 PC 启动器被植入恶意代码。恶意代码是通过纂改 Level Infinite CDN 分发的四个官方 JavaScript 文件实现的，篡改发生于 2026 年 9 月 27 日前后，攻击则始于 2026 年 10 月 23 日到 11 月 3 日，在此期间打开 PC 启动器的用户可能会被植入木马。恶意程序会窃取浏览器保存的密码、Windows 凭据管理器信息、SSH 密钥以及云服务或 AI 服务的访问令牌，还能窃取 28 种基于浏览器的加密货币钱包数据、执行任意命令、读取文件以及屏幕截图。攻击期间打开过启动器的玩家可以打开游戏文件夹，搜寻 debug.log，打开该文件后寻找 k2f_chan，如果找到且显示 registered，那么最好立即卸载游戏并用杀毒软件进行扫描。

items.title: 法国银行被盗走 1.18 亿欧元
items.content_text: 法国国民互助信贷银行（Crédit Mutuel Arkéa）被黑客通过欺诈性交易盗走 1.18 亿欧元。被盗走的钱随后被转移到多个加密货币账号。该银行证实遭到网络攻击，但尚未证实 1.18 亿欧元的数字，只是表示攻击已得到控制，客户不会遭受任何经济损失。国民互助信贷银行暂停了其应用的部分转账功能。

items.title: Firefox 测试迷你窗口功能
items.content_text: Mozilla 正在新版 Firefox Nightly 中测试迷你窗口（Mini Window）功能。该功能类似视频画中画功能，将一个标签页作为独立窗口一直显示在当前标签页之上，这个窗口隐去了地址栏、各类控件、滚动条等常见标签页元素，但如果用户将鼠标悬停在迷你窗口内，各种标签页元素将会显示。迷你窗口方便用户在当前标签页上工作的同时参考迷你窗口的内容，免于在两个标签页之间反复切换。用户可以在专注于当前标签页的同时查看迷你窗口。

items.title: 富士胶片因 AI 热加大磁带产能
items.content_text: 富士胶片表示它将大幅增加磁带产能，原因是磁带备份成为 AI 热的一个意外受益者。普通消费者可能早在几十年前就已不再使用磁带，但业界却从未将其抛弃。云服务巨头依靠磁带对海量数据进行备份。富士胶片称，大型云服务商和数据中心运营商正在扩大对磁带的使用，因为磁带能以相对较低的成本存储海量数据。磁带备份可以轻松与系统断开连接，存放在抽屉、保险库或独立设施内。富士胶片强调，磁带介质能实现物理隔离（air-gap），为用户数据提供最后一道防线。

items.title: Nexus Mods 公布 AI 生成内容政策
items.content_text: 最大 PC 游戏 Mod 分享托管平台 Nexus Mods 公布了 AI 生成内容政策。Nexus Mods 没有禁止 AI 生成 Mod，但对此类 Mod 的分享设定了更严格的规定。新上传 Mod 必须披露是否使用 AI，AI 辅助 Mod 必须说明如何使用 AI 以及 AI 的使用范围。现有 Mod 需在 2027 年 1 月 2 日前符合新要求。如果 Mod 作者无视平台方提出的要求，可能会面临权限受限或被下架的后果。它计划针对 AI 使用、AI 模型训练、分支和衍生 Mod 引入新的授权选项，默认选项为“需征求作者同意（Ask me）”。Nexus Mods 承诺绝不会利用用户上传的 Mod 训练 AI，也不会将其出售或授权给任何 AI 公司。Nexus Mods 严禁利用生成式 AI 生成虚假的游戏截图。

items.title: 苹果开始在中国推出 Apple Intelligence
items.content_text: 苹果从 11 月 4 日起开始在中国推出 AI 功能 Apple Intelligence，中国用户可通过最新的 iOS 开发者 Beta 版进行测试，AI 功能将于 12 月随 iOS 27.3 的发布正式推出。中国版本的 Apple Intelligence 是苹果和阿里巴巴合作推出的，基于阿里巴巴的千问模型。首批 AI 功能包括实时翻译、写作工具、视觉智能、照片 app 的消除工具、智绘表情、照片 app 中的自然语言搜索、在照片 app 中创建回忆影片、识别优先邮件、邮件摘要、智能回复、通知摘要、首要通知、减少干扰、备忘录 app 中的音频转录摘要、通话转录文本的摘要、输⼊⽂字与 Siri 对话、Siri 能接入千问（需登录千问）、创作等。

items.title: 出生前后大脑会清理突变神经元
items.content_text: 根据发表在《自然》上的一项研究，出生前后大脑会清理突变神经元。对 2300 多个神经细胞进行的分析显示，在从人类胎儿大脑中采样的神经元中，超过 1/4 出现了染色体片段增加或缺失的情况。相比之下，出生后婴儿大脑中的神经元中，只有约 6% 存在此类异常。研究结果揭示了一种新的机制，该机制不仅调控着一个人的神经元数量，还决定了哪些胎儿神经元能够在大脑中存活下来。针对小鼠的研究表明，在早期发育过程中，哺乳动物会通过激活一个导致细胞死亡的分子程序，清除大量脑细胞。分析结果显示，在胎儿发育过程中，存在数量惊人的、具有广泛拷贝数变异的细胞。然而出生后，这些异常神经元的比例下降至原来的 1/4，表明它们在发育过程中已被淘汰。大脑是如何分辨哪些神经元正常、哪些不正常呢？一个可能的线索是那些拷贝数变异水平较高的脑细胞，其与其他神经元建立连接（即突触）的基因也往往表现异常。

items.title: SUSE 因 AI 而计划裁员十分之一
items.content_text: 德国开源软件公司 SUSE 现有员工 1900 人，它计划裁掉十分之一的员工。CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen 在电子邮件里表示，自动化和 AI 降低了某些岗位的需求。他表示做出这一决定是非常痛苦的，但也是必要的。Van Leeuwen 称，在被瑞典私募股权投资公司殷拓集团收购后，公司在仔细审视了其未来战略、所需能力及团队架构后做出了裁员决定,“显而易见自动化和 AI 正从根本上改变软件公司的运营方式。AI 技术正呈指数级发展，迫使我们彻底重新构想工作模式。无论是所在行业，还是在更广泛的经济领域，我们都已经看到了这一趋势。这意味着 SUSE 目前所依托的组织架构和成本基础，已无法支撑未来的成功发展。”受影响的员工将在 11 月 4 日前收到通知，员工代表将于次日选出，一对一沟通会议则将于下周初启动。

items.title: Dropping Out of the Electoral College
items.content_text:
The US midterm elections of 2026 have created a new opportunity. The "blue wave" has flipped enough state legislatures that it may be possible to complete the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact and make the Electoral College obsolete.

The NPVIC has a simple plan: all states in the Compact agree to commit their electoral votes to the winner of the popular vote nationwide. But to make it work, there need to be enough states in the Compact to reach 270 votes, the number needed to clinch a presidential election. Looking backward at presidential elections. this system would have had created different outcomes. (Here's a previous discussion on the Blue from 2014 when New York joined, but before the age of Trump). It would also push presidential candidates to shift their focus (and, of course, their money) to larger states, which would upset leaders of the swing states that typically get showered with that attention. The Compact would also need the approval of Congress, but not the President. However, there still aren't enough Democratic senators to overcome a filibuster and pass it.
