items.title: Multifamily CRE Meltdown Keeps Getting Uglier
items.content_text:
Multifamily CRE Meltdown Keeps Getting Uglier

Authored by Wolf Richter via Wolf Street,

There are about $2.3 trillion in multifamily commercial real estate (CRE) loans out there, backed by buildings with rental apartments. The US government, via Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, holds about $1.2 trillion of that. Fannie and Freddie have become very aggressive multifamily CRE lenders. So, dear taxpayer, you're on the hook for about half of the multifamily CRE debt.

The rest is held around the globe by banks, insurance companies, real estate funds, alternative asset managers - a melted-down mortgage just hit Bridge Investment Group, a unit of PE giant Apollo (more on that in a moment) - holders of Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities (CMBS) and Collateralized Loan Obligations (CLOs).

All of them have gotten hit by melted-down mortgages as the higher interest rates make it just about impossible to refinance the balloon payments when they come due on fixed-rate loans, or even make interest payments on variable-rate loans pegged to SOFR, which jumped when the Fed started hiking its policy rates. The result has been wave after wave of multifamily defaults, and it keeps getting worse.

CMBS holders got hit by another default: The $210 million interest-only 5-year mortgage on a Class A 283-unit 20-acre waterfront apartment property, "The Cove at Tiburon," across the Bay from San Francisco. The mortgage had been issued in 2020 to refinance the property at ultra-low interest rates. The mortgage was then securitized and sold to investors who thought that ultra-low interest rates would be a permanent feature.

The interest-only mortgage became delinquent when it wasn't paid off in October, after having already been modified and extended in November 2025. It could not be refinanced at current interest rates because the declining rental income wasn't enough to cover operating expenses and the interest payments at today's interest rates. Now there are talks underway to extend it for another six months, according to Trepp, which analyzes and tracks CMBS. Extend and pretend forevermore.

The multifamily CMBS delinquency rate rose to 8.1% in October, driven by this delinquency, the highest since 2016, when the $3 billion delinquent loan on the huge 11,250-apartment campus, Stuyvesant Town - Peter Cooper Village, in Manhattan, was paid off by the acquirers of the property.

Back in 2024, Morningstar DBRS, which rated the CMBS, wrote about the problems lining up for the mortgage on The Cove at Tiburon:

"At issuance [of the loan in 2020], Morningstar DBRS shadow-rated the loan investment grade given that the property benefits from a prime waterfront location, superior amenities, and limited competition within the submarket. However, despite these aspects, which Morningstar DBRS expected to contribute to cash flow stability over the loan term, the property's reported occupancy rate and cash flow trended downward shortly after issuance, primarily as a result of a slowdown in leasing activity....

"As per the March 2024 rent roll, the property was 80.2% occupied at an average rental rate of $5,789 per unit, compared with June 2022 figures of 91.9% and $5,852 per unit, respectively.

"It appears that new leases are being signed at lower rental rates to curb increases in vacancy rates, resulting in lowered cash flows...."

And now that property would have to be refinanced at much higher interest rates, and that just doesn't pencil out.

Other lenders got hit too.

Bridge Investment Group, an alternative investment manager owned by PE giant Apollo, is now stuck with the defaulted $360 million loan on The Beaudry, a new high-end 64-floor apartment tower in downtown Los Angeles, with 785 units and amenities such as floor-to-ceiling windows, saltwater pool, spa, rooftop lounge, 24/7 athletic club, a full-swing golf simulator, etc.

The tower, which opened in 2023, was developed by giant real-estate developer and landlord Brookfield for about $600 million. Because the $360 million loan cannot be refinanced at today's interest rates without a massive capital infusion, Brookfield decided to hand over the keys, walk away from the property and the loan, and let the lender worry about the whole schmear, according to the WSJ today.

Brookfield, which already defaulted on mortgages of numerous office towers in Los Angeles and around the country, has played a substantial role in the Office CRE meltdown.

Bridge Investment Group is now trying to sell the Beaudry loan - and thereby the rights to the property.

The Beaudry has lots of competition: Over 10,000 new apartments were built from 2017 to 2021 in downtown L.A., the most of any other downtown in the country, according to RentCafe, cited by the WSJ.

Then came working from home, and proximity to now substantially vacant and defaulting office towers wasn't such a magnet anymore.

At the Beaudry, rents start at $2,424 a month for a 539-square-foot studio on the sixth floor, according to its website. Up the scale, a two-bedroom 1,200 sf apartment on the eighth floor is listed at $4,905. The same floorplan on the 20th floor is listed at $5,730. A 3-bedroom 1,700 sf unit on the 49th floor is listed at $8,893. All of them with big views.

Asking rents average around $4,200 a month at the Beaudry, according to CoStar, cited by the WSJ, far below what Brookfield had aimed for. "A lot of students live here," Max Xing, a student at the University of Southern California, told the WSJ. He moved into a studio in August. But the Beaudry was designed as high-end living for professionals working downtown, Andrew Parks, a lead designer on the Beaudry, told the WSJ. "We wanted to go for something that felt very sophisticated."

In addition to the higher interest rates...

There are other pieces to the multifamily meltdown, including:

Growing supply: The Growth of the Vacant Housing Stock in the US

And pressure on multifamily rents: Single-Family & Multifamily Rents in the US and 22 Large US Metros

items.title: Ex-School Board President Indicted In Alleged $1.3 Million Kickback Over $2.7 Million COVID-Funded Air Purifier Deal
items.content_text:
Ex-School Board President Indicted In Alleged $1.3 Million Kickback Over $2.7 Million COVID-Funded Air Purifier Deal

A federal grand jury in Chicago has indicted Annette Johnson, the former president of the East Aurora School District 131 Board of Education, on charges that she entered the district into a $2.7 million air purifier purchase in 2021 in exchange for a $1.3 million payment. Johnson, 63, of Aurora, faces two counts of honest services mail fraud and one count of honest services wire fraud, each punishable by up to 20 years in federal prison, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Illinois said. She remains a member of the board.

Prosecutors say that Johnson, then board president, voted for the purchase, and that the district paid for the purifiers with COVID-era federal grant money. Unbeknownst to the other board members, they say, Johnson and the vendor had agreed that the vendor would pay more than $1 million of the sale proceeds to a company owned by her boyfriend, where she served as chief financial officer.

Within days of a board vote in which Johnson participated and approved payment, prosecutors say, the vendor mailed a $1.3 million check labeled "commission" to that company. Later, she allegedly pushed the board to approve a $201,077 payment to the vendor in 2023 for an "extended warranty" on the purifiers. The US Attorney's office does not name the vendor nor the company in the complaint, and Johnson was the only person indicted.

The indictment also accuses Johnson of failing to list $7,500 paid to her in 2021 by a company involved in the deal on her statement of economic interests. Johnson said in a statement Monday that she recognizes the gravity of the allegations. "I maintain my innocence of the criminal charges brought against me, and I intend to vigorously defend myself through the judicial process," she said, according to the Sun-Times.

Aurora Mayor John Laesch told the Sun-Times that a whistleblower approached him in 2024 and that district records show eight companies with purported ties to Johnson received $43.1 million from the district between 2018 and 2023, which he says he gave to prosecutors. He has called on her to resign, the paper reported. The $43.1 million figure is Laesch's claim, not an allegation in the indictment.

The same report says Johnson's economic-interest statements were blank from 2012 to 2024 and that she first listed a company, DJ Payne Corporation, in 2025. A 2024 challenge to her candidacy over the filings was dismissed after the board ruled it lacked authority to review them.

The district said Johnson, like any defendant, is entitled to a presumption of innocence. Officials told the Sun-Times it is working with investigators. An indictment is not evidence of guilt, and Johnson is presumed innocent. Her term on the board runs through April 2029, according to the district's website, and the Sun-Times reports she is due in court Nov. 9.

UCLA Cops Stockpile Drones And Less-Lethal Munitions For 'Emergency Incidents'

Authored by Bryan Hyde via American Greatness,

The UCLA Police Department (UCPD) spent more than $220,000 on drones and less-than-lethal munitions in 2025 and is now seeking approval to expand its inventory further.

An Oct. 19 military equipment report reveals that UCPD bought three Skydio X10s under a 10-year contract at a cost of $21,654 annually for the drones and their docking stations.

According to the Daily Bruin, the drones are part of UCPD's new Drone as First Responder program.

Richard Mejia, director of emergency communications and information for the Office of Campus and Community Safety, said in an emailed statement that the program aims to "improve situational awareness, reduce response times and provide valuable video evidence during emergency incidents."

According to UCPD's report, the $220k expenditure covered a variety of specialized security equipment including drones, less-than-lethal munitions such as 40 millimeter sponge rounds and projectile launchers as well as long-range acoustic devices.

The Daily Bruin reports the department also owns semiautomatic patrol rifles but categorizes them as "standard issue service weapons" rather than military equipment, per the report.

The Skydio X10, launched in Sept. 2023, is a quadcopter with a folding design which, according to the manufacturer, can be made flight-ready from a backpack in 40 seconds.

UCPD purchased 120 40 mm munitions in 2025 and owns 3,117 less-than-lethal munitions in total and the department is requesting 1,950 additional PepperBall rounds and 50 more 40 mm projectiles, according to the report.

The report states:

All additional equipment is necessary to support the department's growth and expansion due to UCLA's acquisition/construction of additional University-owned housing, medical, and administrative properties, as well as in preparation for the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

According to the report, which must be published and submitted to the UC Board of Regents annually, UCPD did not use its military equipment outside of training purposes in 2025.

The most recent disclosure has fueled significant debate across the University of California system.

EdSource reports that faculty groups, student organizations, and civil liberties advocates have expressed deep concerns over the "militarization" of campus security, arguing that these stockpiles could be used to suppress peaceful student protests rather than protect the community.

UCLA professor Michael Chwe launched a petition that has gathered hundreds of campus signatures demanding that police stop using 40mm launchers altogether, according to the NY Post.

items.title: House Democrats Eye Their Own Crypto Market Structure Bill With A Bigger SEC Role After Sweep
items.content_text:
House Democrats Eye Their Own Crypto Market Structure Bill With A Bigger SEC Role After Sweep

Authored by Micah Zimmerman via Bitcoin Magazine,

House Democrats are discussing a plan to turn Rep. Maxine Waters' Crypto Investor and Consumer Bill of Rights into their own crypto market structure bill next Congress, with ideas that include a bigger role for the SEC and a smaller one for the CFTC, Eleanor Terrett reported Wednesday.

🚨SCOOP: House Democrats are discussing plans to expand the Crypto Investor and Consumer Bill of Rights, @RepMaxineWaters' amendment to the Clarity Act in 2025, into a broader crypto "market structure" bill next Congress.

The proposal would fold in Democratic Clarity Act...

— Eleanor Terrett (@EleanorTerrett) November 4, 2026

The proposal would fold in the Democratic Clarity Act provisions Waters offered in the House, which were not adopted, plus the provisions Senate Democrats were able to agree on with Republicans before September's failed cloture vote. Terrett cited three industry sources who have spoken with Democratic staffers.

Further ethics provisions restricting the crypto activities of President Donald Trump and other federal officials are also likely, she wrote. Republicans are calling it a "messaging bill."

No text for the crypto market structure bill has been released, and the details so far come from industry sources rather than from lawmakers.

JUST IN: 🇺🇸 House Democrats reportedly want to revive their Clarity Act provisions in a broader crypto market structure bill next Congress, Eleanor Terrett reports. 👀 pic.twitter.com/8twokppjHz

— Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 4, 2026

The talks follow Tuesday's Democratic sweep of Congress. Waters, the top Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee, is in line to take the gavel in January from Chairman French Hill, the Clarity Act's sponsor.

Bloomberg Law reported Wednesday that the new majorities give Democrats leverage over the Clarity Act, the industry's top legislative priority, starting with tougher ethics rules aimed at Trump's ventures.

What the Waters amendment would do for crypto

Waters offered the bill of rights as amendment #31 to H.R. 3633 in July 2025. The House Rules Committee blocked it 4-8 along party lines, on a motion from Rep. Mary Gay Scanlon of Pennsylvania. Making an amendment "in order" lets the full House debate and vote on it, so the result kept the package off the floor.

The committee's record lists what it would have required: 24/7 customer service, insurance or SIPC-like coverage, fiduciary and best-execution rules, anti-front-running rules, bankruptcy-remote custody with 24-hour withdrawals and monthly auditor-attested proof of reserves. It would also have sent more funding to the SEC and CFTC.

The committee rejected a second Democratic amendment by the same 4-8 margin. That one, from Rep. Joe Neguse of Colorado, would have barred members of Congress, presidents and vice presidents from issuing or endorsing digital assets. The ethics fight it previewed later followed the bill to the Senate.

SEC versus CFTC

The agency split is where a Democratic crypto market structure bill would break most sharply from the Republican one. The House-passed Clarity Act directs the CFTC to regulate most digital commodity trading, including exchanges, brokers and dealers, and exempts tokens on mature blockchains from SEC registration under certain conditions.

That design is the one the industry backed. A crypto market structure bill that moves supervision back toward the SEC would reverse it.

The Clarity Act passed the House 294-134 in July 2025 and failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15. Sen. Thom Tillis entered a motion to reconsider, which preserves the option of another vote, but the bill dies when this Congress ends on Jan. 3 unless the lame-duck session revives it.

Democrats now hold the leverage. "The industry and the Republicans screwed up. That was the best bill they were going to get," Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona, a Senate Banking Committee member, said in comments reported by Bloomberg Law.

TD Cowen's Jaret Seiberg wrote Wednesday that the sweep closes the door on Clarity for two years, and that Democratic investigations of the Trump family's crypto ventures "may make it impossible to advance a version of Clarity that the crypto sector could back."

A Democratic crypto market structure bill would still need Trump's signature to become law. Whether one built around the SEC can draw enough Republican votes to get there, or remains the messaging bill Republicans say it is, is the question the next Congress opens with.

Intel's China Problem Just Got A Lot Worse

Huawei unveiled its first desktop computer running its own HarmonyOS operating system on Thursday, a machine with no Intel or Qualcomm chip and no Windows, which the South China Morning Post reported is 100% domestically made.

The Qingyun HM650 made its debut at the HarmonyOS Office Industry Summit in Wuhan, where Zhu Dongdong, president of Huawei's tablet and PC product line, laid out the specs. It runs on Huawei's Kirin X90, a 10-core, 20-thread processor rated at 40 watts, well under the 65 to 125 watts typical of desktop processors, with Huawei's Maleoon 910 graphics, and carries what the company calls a "100% localization certification." Huawei said tighter integration of its hardware and software lifts overall system performance by 15%.

The machine ships with an enterprise edition of HarmonyOS and a dedicated key for Huawei's Celia AI assistant. Huawei is pitching it to finance, enterprise and energy customers, and gave no price or sale date.

No Intel, no Qualcomm: Huawei unveils desktop built entirely with China-made components: SCMP.

Goodbye China market

— zerohedge (@zerohedge) November 5, 2026

Huawei said at the summit that cumulative shipments of HarmonyOS computers have passed one million units. The company shipped 141,000 HarmonyOS PCs in all of 2025, according to figures cited by TechRadar in March.

Forced Out Of Wintel

In May 2024, Washington revoked the export licenses that let Intel and Qualcomm sell chips to Huawei, which had used Intel's Core processors in most of its consumer laptops. Huawei's license to put Microsoft Windows on its PCs expired in March 2025.

Huawei launched its first HarmonyOS laptops two months later. At a July briefing in Beijing, Zhu said the lineup now runs from the MateBook 14 to the 18-inch MateBook Fold, with the Qingyun line for government and business, and that native HarmonyOS PC apps had grown from about 1,000 at launch to more than 19,000.

Huawei had sold desktops without Intel inside before. Its earlier Qingyun machines ran Kirin chips on Chinese Linux distributions, as Tom's Hardware reported. The HM650 is the first to run Huawei's own operating system, which passed a Level II "secure and reliable" certification from China's national information security evaluation center when Huawei showed the desktop in September, IT Home reported.

When TechInsights tore down the Kirin X90 in last year's MateBook Fold, it found the chip was built on SMIC's 7nm (N+2) process, the same node that first appeared in the Mate 60 Pro in August 2023, rather than the rumored 5nm. The firm said SMIC's 5nm process remained elusive and that a Huawei stuck at 7nm is "multiple generations behind" the leading chipmakers.

As we noted in May, Huawei's answer is what it calls a Tau scaling law: its semiconductor chief, He Tingbo, laid out a "LogicFolding" architecture meant to cut signal delay and raise transistor density, with 1.4nm chips targeted by 2031. SMIC shares jumped more than 18% to a record on the news.

'Safe and Reliable'

Beijing has ordered government agencies and party organs above the township level to buy "safe and reliable" processors and operating systems, as we reported seemingly eons and epochs ago in March 2024, steering them away from Intel, AMD and Windows. The approved list, all Chinese, is kept by the China Information Technology Security Evaluation Center, which certified the Kirin X90 in March 2025. State-owned enterprises were reportedly told to finish switching to domestic suppliers by 2027.

China was Intel's largest market in 2023, accounting for 27% of its $54 billion in sales. Qualcomm says in its fiscal 2025 annual report that it derives "a significant portion" of its revenue from Chinese device makers, that it expects no further product revenue from Huawei, and that some of its Chinese customers have developed their own chips.

Huawei is working on the machines that make the chips, too. As we reported in September, it has taken the coordinating role in China's push to build its own DUV lithography tools, funding lens and light-source suppliers through its venture arms, while China's two biggest memory makers, CXMT and YMTC, stockpiled enough ASML equipment to cover about three years of expansion.

items.title: Hedge Fund Walleye Returns Capital, Fires Head Of Equities After Worst Month Since COVID: Read The Full Letter
items.content_text:
Hedge Fund Walleye Returns Capital, Fires Head Of Equities After Worst Month Since COVID: Read The Full Letter

One week ago, when Nomura's Charlie McElligott told clients that the October "pod purge" was the multi-strat model simply "cleansing" itself, we were less sanguine: "we suspect the next round of stop-outs is probably just a matter of time." Well, Charlie was wrong, we were right: it took about a week. And this time it's an entire fund.

Moments ago, Bloomberg reported that Walleye Capital, the $17 billion multistrategy hedge fund run by CIO Will England, is returning a portion of its capital to investors and gutting its internal equities business after its worst month since March 2020. Walleye lost 5.9% in October, bringing its 2026 losses through last month to 6.8%, according to people familiar. Anil Gondi, the firm's head of equities, has been let go along with a "substantial" portion of the internal long/short teams, according to a letter sent to investors on Thursday, which we have obtained and post in full below.

Here is the math: if October's 5.9% loss took Walleye to -6.8% YTD, the fund was down roughly 1% for the year going into the month. That's the "already challenging 2026" England references in his first paragraph. Then October turned a mediocre year into a bad one.

"Not Going To Be Trying To Replicate" Millennium

The letter is short, and unusually blunt for a hedge fund letter. England opens with "discipline, humility, and self-awareness" and then gets right to the point:

Following our worst month since March 2020, in an already challenging 2026, we have taken a hard look at every aspect of our firm. With that in mind, we are simplifying our internal equity long/short business. This decision includes parting ways with our long/short leadership and a substantial portion of our internal long/short investment teams. We are also going to lean into the businesses where we have a proven and differentiated right to win, including our Volatility, Quant and external businesses. Related, we have evaluated the optimal size of the Fund and plan to return a portion of our capital.

Investors will hear later about "the quantum, timing, and mechanics" of the capital return. As for why, England writes that internal equity L/S has been Walleye's weakest strategy since 2023 and "substantially underperformed" the firm's external long/short business (i.e., the outside managers Walleye allocates to). Several years and a new leadership team later:

Those efforts did not produce the results we expected, and the opportunity cost and resources consumed have been too high relative to the return. It did, however, reinforce an important lesson: our competitive advantage is not going to be trying to replicate the traditional multi-manager equity long/short model.

In other words, a $17 billion fund just admitted it can't out-pod the pod shops, at least not in single-stock long/short, where Millennium, Citadel, Balyasny and Point72 are all bidding for the same PMs and crowding into the same trades.

The irony is that Walleye spent the past 18 months trying to do exactly that. Gondi, a former Balyasny PM, was hired in 2025 to lead the equities unit, in the same overhaul in which Walleye dismissed its credit and commodities teams to focus on volatility, quant and fundamental long/short. As recently as mid-October, trade press reported Walleye was still building out its equities business under Gondi, adding Balyasny's chief equities strategist and a Millennium recruiter. Meanwhile, the equity unit's COO had already left in September to return to Citadel, per Hedgeweek. Three weeks is a long time in pod land.

Walleye isn't quitting stocks entirely. It will keep allocating to external long/short managers "as we have for over 10 years," keep its day-one seeding of new managers (with a nod to the "natural strategic alignment" with Dockside, the platform it launched in 2023 to connect investors with smaller managers), and keep its "highest conviction" internal PMs, who will now report directly to England. Partners Tom and Chris "will step back into the management of this external long/short business, reporting to me as they did before in 2024 and most of 2025." Translation: the old org chart is back, minus the people hired to replace it.

From "No New Cash" To "Here's Some Cash Back"

The more interesting line is the one about size. Back in July 2025, Walleye stopped taking money from new investors after a capital raise, with England writing that the strategies needed time to "settle at their new size." At the time, the fund managed a little over $8 billion. Today it manages more than $17 billion. So assets more than doubled in about 16 months, and the fund has now decided the "optimal size" is smaller than what it has.

That's precisely the dynamic McElligott described in his "CLEANSING" note (available to pro subs), which we covered in "The Pod Purge Will Pass" last week: asset growth in multi-strats, "the near pervasive demand for bodies to fill seats to manage that money (potentially 'talent dilutive')," and the leverage the model requires create "'Perpetual Crowding'-risk" and "periods of rolling stop-outs." Walleye just ran that diagnosis on itself: too much money, chasing too few good stock-pickers, in the most crowded corner of the market.

And England's letter has one more tell. The volatility business, he writes, had its strongest month on record in October and is on track for its best year ever in dollar P&L. If the vol book had a record month and the whole fund still lost 5.9%, then the rest of the book lost a lot more than 5.9%.

Not all of that was the stock pickers. England concedes quant had "a softer 2026," which is putting it gently given what happened to systematic funds last month. As we reported on Tuesday, Goldman's Prime Brokerage "October 2026: First Look on Hedge Fund Performance and Positioning" (available to pro subs) showed Systematic L/S funds lost 3.6% in October, "the first down month since Jul '25 and the worst monthly drawdown in six years," with quant alpha a staggering -5.06%. The light blue line on the left shows the quants' entire YTD lead evaporating in the last two weeks of the month:

Nowhere To Hide

Walleye was hardly alone. As we detailed in "Nowhere To Hide" on Tuesday, global Fundamental L/S funds lost 3.49% in October while quants lost 3.6%, the first time on Goldman's record (going back to 2016) that both cohorts lost 3% or more in the same month:

Goldman's other observation now looks prescient: the asset-weighted return (-3.49%) was far worse than the median (-1.69%), "suggesting large managers underperformed." Ten months into the year, the median fundamental L/S fund was up just 1.16% vs 10.89% for the MSCI World, and the bottom quartile was down 9.88%. Walleye, at -6.8%, sits a lot closer to the bottom quartile than to the median:

Bloomberg's tally of the big names tells the same story. Millennium lost 2.3% in October, ExodusPoint 2.4%, Marshall Wace's Eureka 5.4%, and credit fund Arini was on track for its worst month ever, down 12.1% through Oct 23. And just this afternoon, Bloomberg reported that Greg Coffey's Kirkoswald had its worst month ever, losing about 6.4% on the back of Brazil's election whiplash and breaking a 16-month winning streak. The lone giant in the green was, naturally, Citadel, up 1.7% in its flagship Wellington fund. Which is also where Walleye's equity COO went back to in September. Funny how that works.

As JPMorgan's positioning intelligence team put it, "October is a month that most hedge funds will probably want to forget." Walleye apparently decided forgetting wasn't enough.

...And November Isn't Helping

The timing of the letter (Thursday, with the market in freefall) is probably not entirely a coincidence either. As we noted earlier today, UBS trader Torsten Sippel said hedge funds opened the session 23/75 buy/sell, with the "clearest sign of capitulation" in neoclouds and semis, while Goldman's John Flood reported that "our phones are exploding" with requests for color, and "we are not seeing buyers step in to defend anything just yet."

Most relevant for Walleye's peers, Goldman's Prime Brokerage (Marco Laicini) had this snapshot as of mid-morning:

U.S. markets sell-off and global momentum down. Fundamentals down with US-focused funds hit harder. TMT severely down. Systematics are positive, and multi-strategy funds down significantly on their equity exposure.

So that's two bad days in a row for the pods' equity books, right as allocators read Walleye's letter and start asking their own managers some uncomfortable questions about "optimal size."

Recall that by headhunters' count, roughly 100 PMs were already out of a job in October (vs. ~40 in September and ~20 before that), per eFinancialCareers, with one PM complaining that "hedge funds hired too many morons." Walleye's cuts will add to that tally, though for once the purge came from the top of the org chart rather than the bottom.

The First To Hand Back The Money, Probably Not The Last

England frames the move as "proactive," noting that "several of our largest partners" encouraged the simplification, and that investor demand for Walleye's vol, quant and external strategies remains strong. Maybe. But a fund that closed its doors to new money 16 months ago to let its strategies "settle at their new size" is now shrinking after its worst month since the COVID crash, and that's hard to spin as anything other than a retreat.

McElligott's view last week was that this "too shall pass," the model "cleansing the excess Positioning and Leverage out of the system." We remain skeptical: with gross leverage in the 97th percentile on Goldman's five-year lookback, nets near one-year lows, the median fund barely positive for the year and the year-end clock ticking, the cleansing has so far come from PMs being stopped out, while gross has barely moved. Walleye returning capital is the first sign that allocators, and the platforms themselves, are starting to shrink the capital base too. That's the part of the cycle where "get smaller" finally happens, and it's rarely orderly.

Or, as England himself put it, "our competitive advantage is not going to be trying to replicate the traditional multi-manager equity long/short model." A lot of mid-sized multi-strats which spent the past three years trying to do just that may soon be reaching the same conclusion... and writing similar letters.

The Full Walleye Letter

items.title: Tuttle Files For New Credit Default Swap ETFs To Bet Against AI Debt
items.content_text:
Tuttle Files For New Credit Default Swap ETFs To Bet Against AI Debt

Tuttle Capital Management has filed with the SEC to launch five new ETFs that would give everyday investors exposure to a growing concern on Wall Street: the massive amounts of debt being taken on to finance the AI boom, according to the SEC Prospectus. 

The proposed funds would target Oracle (ORCL), CoreWeave (CRWV), the Magnificent Seven tech giants, semiconductor companies, and hyperscalers building large-scale computing infrastructure. The filings come as investors increasingly question whether the hundreds of billions being spent on AI data centers, chips, and cloud infrastructure will generate enough revenue to justify the investment.

Unlike traditional ETFs that aim to profit from rising stock prices, these funds would use credit default swaps (CDS), financial contracts that work like insurance against corporate debt defaults. 

When investors become more concerned about a company's ability to repay its debt, the cost of that insurance typically rises. Tuttle's ETFs would aim to profit from that increase, even if the underlying companies never actually default. The proposed funds would also use leverage of 5 to 10 times their assets to amplify exposure to changes in credit risk, making them particularly risky investments. 

Essentially, they would allow investors to bet that the market is underestimating the financial risks behind the AI buildout.

We previously predicted that CDS trader could be the best job of 2027, as the AI investment boom creates growing demand for ways to insure and trade risky corporate debt. Tuttle's filing is another sign that this market could expand beyond specialized Wall Street trading desks and become accessible to everyday investors. 

While the products have yet to launch, their proposed introduction suggests that asset managers see an opportunity in growing concerns about AI financing. For years, the biggest AI trade was betting on the companies that would benefit from the technology. 

As we have often joked (kind of...) the next big opportunity may be betting on the rising cost of insuring the debt used to build it.

El-Sayed named Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) as the Democrat he would prefer to see run for majority leader. Reports have indicated that Van Hollen is weighing a 2028 presidential campaign.

"I'd love to see him run," El-Sayed said of Van Hollen. "It seems that he has his sights set on another prize. But I've been very clear that I think we need new leadership."

El-Sayed did not commit to any candidate. "But a vote is a choice between two options," he said of the leadership race. "I don't know what the options are right now. So let's see who comes out of the woodwork and is excited to lead."

The incoming senator's stance puts him at odds with the leader who backed his general election campaign. Schumer did not start out in El-Sayed's corner. In the Democratic primary, Schumer first supported El-Sayed's rival, Rep. Haley Stevens (D-MI) of Birmingham. After El-Sayed won the nomination, Schumer threw his support behind him.

Frustration with Schumer's leadership has simmered among Democrats in recent years, even as the party flipped at least seven Republican-held seats. He addressed that criticism Wednesday at a press conference at the headquarters of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee.

"This is not about me ... This is about the American people and what they want and what they need and what we can do to help them. Plain and simple," Schumer said.

Schumer needs only a majority of the Democratic caucus to keep his post, and current projections put the caucus at 54 to 56 members in 2027.

"The issue is not me. I'll be reelected as majority leader. But the issue is focusing on the American people and what they want," Schumer told reporters.

Senate Democrats hold their leadership elections next month.

items.title: Outcome Of Alaska Senate Race May Not Be Known For Weeks
items.content_text:
Outcome Of Alaska Senate Race May Not Be Known For Weeks

Authored by Mark Stricherz via The Center Square,

The outcome of a tightly contested and controversial U.S. Senate race in Alaska may not be known until the end of the month or later.

U.S. Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, a Republican, is making a bid for a third six-year term. As of 1400ET today, he trails former U.S. Rep. Mary Peltola, a Democrat, by 637 votes with 74% of ballots counted. He has 102,325 votes to her 102,962. 

The race has been the focus of controversy after The New York Times reported that Peltola's campaign helped recruit a candidate with the same name as Sullivan in an apparent attempt to confuse voters. She has denied doing that.

Two Senate races are still uncalled, and both could break Democrats' way.

Democrat Scott Colom is all but declaring victory in his challenge to Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-Miss.), in what would be yet another Senate stunner for Democrats. In Alaska, the count is still dragging on... pic.twitter.com/7PYiu5jGx4

— Punchbowl News (@PunchbowlNews) November 4, 2026

Twenty-three percent of votes have yet to be tallied. Even when they are, the narrow margin separating the candidates means that the outcome may be decided not at the state's polling sites but through the mail via absentee and questioned ballots.

In the previous midterm congressional election four years ago, Alaska officials said they received 9,143 in-person absentee ballots and 8,009 questioned ballots. Two years ago, in the presidential election, state officials reported receiving 18,158 in-person absentee ballots and 15,138 questioned ballots. Voters can ask for a mail-in ballot and still vote in person, so the number of outstanding votes in the state's general elections in 2022 and 2024 is unclear.

Steve Kirch, public relations manager for the state's division of elections, did not immediately return an interview request.

What is clear is the 49th state's deadline for counting all votes.

By Nov. 13, absentee ballots from the 50 states plus its territories as well as Puerto Rico, Guam, the Virgin Islands, and American Samoa should have arrived and must be postmarked by Nov. 3. By Nov. 18, all ballots from overseas addresses must be received and postmarked by Election Day. By Nov. 19, the State Review Board begins its review of election materials, and by Nov. 25, state officials expect to certify the election results.

In addition, Alaska has ranked choice voting. Peltola or Sullivan will need to receive more than 50 percent of the first-choice votes after officials have counted them all. If neither does, the last-place candidate is eliminated. Then, state officials redistribute that candidate's ballots according to voters' second and subsequent choices. The process continues until a candidate receives a majority, or 50% plus one vote.

Despite the state's deadlines, federal officials may complicate them.

The Justice Department has sent a target letter to prominent Democratic elections attorney Marc Elias asking about his possible involvement in petitioning a retired teacher by the name of Dan J. Sullivan to run for Alaska's Senate seat, according to the Associated Press.

Audrey Cook, a spokesman for the Justice Department, told The Center Square that the agency "cannot discuss ongoing investigations."

Deepwater's Munster: AI Is "Different This Time"

Last night's ZeroHedge Debate brought together AI bull Gene Munster and veteran investor (and AI bear) George Noble for a clash over whether the AI-driven stock market rally is another speculative bubble or the beginning of a much larger technological revolution.

Munster argued that AI really is "different this time," with adoption and corporate spending poised to grow far beyond current expectations. Noble pushed back, warning that massive capital expenditures, mounting debt, and questionable returns on investment bear troubling similarities to past bubbles.

We recommend watching the full debate, but here are the highlights for those who missed it:

Munster: AI Is "Different This Time"

A famous Apple-bull in the 2010s (an trade that’s looking pretty good at today’s valuations), Munster dismissed the Dot-Com scare that Noble and others are applying to the AI bull run:

"I'm careful when I say that this is different, but this is different. What's going on right now in AI, the significance of it is hard, I think, for humans to wrap our minds around."

The bull thesis rests on AI spending to grow as adoption spreads across industries, particularly those dependent on knowledge work… and the average AI model now has an IQ of 130, compared to the average human with 100.

"There's $150 billion or $300 billion between OpenAI and Anthropic, $300 billion gonna be spent in the next 12 months from enterprise customers. That's real spending. But that still doesn't answer the question: how do you get from $300 billion to trillions of spending?"

Munster compared corporate AI-spending relative to traditional software (SaaS), citing a wide divide that, if closed, could mean a growth of several multiples for the AI sector.

"The average spend on AI per employee is 25 bucks a month right now. The average spend on, if you look at software, is $700. So this has so much room to grow…  the next three to five years are going to surprise people, not just surprise, shock people at how resilient the AI trade is."

pic.twitter.com/jDXheNWV6J

— ZeroHedge Debates (@zerohedgeDebate) November 5, 2026

George keeping TSLAQ alive 

Noble drew on his experience shorting Tesla to challenge Munster's reliance on long-term growth projections, arguing that optimistic forecasts mean little if the underlying financial performance fails to materialize.

"I will freely admit that I lost money in the past shorting Tesla, but I also happily report that this year has worked out pretty well so far."

"If you look at not only the Tesla revenues [being] way off, but even worse, the margins associated with those revenues, it's been a complete and utter disaster."

The same risk, he argued, applies to AI companies whose valuations depend heavily on earnings projected (emphasis on projected) years into the future.

"I get in a bull market where people are extending time horizons and cost of capital is at a minimum, dreams have more appeal." But with capital becoming more expensive, Noble suggested that credit markets may be less willing to finance those ambitions.

"They always say the bond guys are smarter than the equity guys. Bond guys are like, 'You've got some explaining to do.' The equity guys are the dreamers… doesn't matter what I think, the market is not buying what you're selling."

items.content_text: 印度计算机应急响应小组（CERT-In）星期三发布安全通报，被称为“狡猾猎鹰”（Crafty Falcon）的黑客组织，已入侵非银行贷款机构、金融科技公司及加密货币交易所。攻击者利用公开可用的 AI 工具，实现高速自动化入侵。印度计算机应急响应小组形容这项威胁“仍在发生，且持续活跃”。该机构点名四款用于入侵的工具，分别是 ARTEX、PentAGI、Cairn 和 CyberStrikeAI。ARTEX 此前曾被用于攻击韩国银行。印度计算机应急响应小组没有说明这些攻击事件由谁发动，也未透露该组织的运作地点。该机构也没有称这些攻击由国家支持或主导，且其点名的攻击工具均可在网络上免费获取。

items.title: 同步导致电网呈现周期为一分钟的震荡
items.content_text: 今天的电网接入了数以百万计的数字控制设备，为了维持电力供需平衡，精准预测和实时控制必不可少。电力系统因此转变成为一种信息物理融合的基础设施（Cyber–Physical Infrastructure）。物理设备与数字控制系统之间形成了紧密的相互依存关系，在带来前所未有的效率与灵活性的同时也引入了新的系统性风险。根据发表在《Nature Energy》期刊上的一项研究，德国研究人员指出全球电力系统存在的一种由信息物理同步效应所引发的、周期为一分钟的相干振荡现象。除了故障和恶意攻击外，即使是良性的控制程序，当大量设备以协同一致的方式运行时，也可能产生系统层面的影响。在大规模信息物理能源系统中，非预期的同步行为可能引发反复出现且具有潜在放大效应的振荡现象。

items.title: 越南对足球直播盗版者判刑最高一年
items.content_text: 越南一家法院对 14 名参与盗版足球赛事直播网站 Bun Cha TV 的团队判处最高一年徒刑。4 名内容、编程和运营团队负责人被判处 12 个月徒刑，另外 5 人判处 10 个月监禁，2 人判处 8 个月监禁，3 名解说员被判处 10 个月缓刑。所有 14 名被告都承认了指控，配合了调查。Bun Cha TV 累计直播逾 15 万场体育赛事，通过博彩及赌博广告非法获利逾 200 亿越南盾（约 512 万人民币）。内容团队负责人获利逾 4.3 亿越南盾，解说员非法所得则在 3100 万到 4.8 亿越南盾不等。美国 MPAA 的代表称赞了这一判决。

items.title: 白宫网络监测到住宅代理活动
items.content_text: 安全公司 Layer3 Intel 报告，他们在分配给白宫的自治系统 AS2650 中监测到住宅代理服务的活动。住宅代理服务会将用户的网络地址租给其他人使用。Layer3 在 10 月 5 日-11 月 3 日期间观察到了 236 次住宅代理连接活动。住宅代理的源头被认为来自 Windows 11 设备安装的俄罗斯代理程序 Infatica。Layer3 Intel 指出，在30 天内有 26 天出现了源自白宫的代理出口节点流量，涉及 6 个 IP，大部分活动发生在傍晚，即下午 5 点至午夜之间。

items.title: Bazzite 45 释出
items.content_text: 基于 Fedora 的游戏发行版 Bazzite 释出了 v45。主要变化包括；基于 Fedora 45，更新 Open Gaming Collective(OGC)内核，支持罗技 TrueWheel 设备等等。过去几年 Linux 对游戏的支持有了显著改善，但对很多用户而言仍然需要自行配置。Bazzite 项目旨在让 Linux 桌面用户无需额外配置就能畅玩游戏，设计类似 Valve 的 SteamOS，但更适合通用桌面使用情景：SteamOS 主要支持 AMD GPU，Bazzite 包含了私有的 NVIDIA 驱动。

items.title: Google 和 OpenAI 的模型对特定口音有偏见
items.content_text: 研究人员调查了先进多模态模型如何评估面试、会议报告和英语口语能力测试中的语音，测试的模型包括了 Google 的 Gemini 2.5 Pro 和 Gemini 2.5 Flash，以及 OpenAI 的 GPT-Audio 1.5，开放权重模型 Qwen 3 Omni。这些模型对五种不同口音——美国、英国、中国、印度和尼日利亚——的英语语音进行了评分。AI 模型普遍将中国和尼日利亚口音的评分最低，印度口音居中，美国和英国口音的评分最高。即使内容完全相同，系统仍然认为美国和英国口音的表达方式和内容都更胜一筹。研究团队发现，明显的等级划分也体现在模型的解释中。研究人员说，模型反复声称中国和尼日利亚口音的英语使用者含糊不清或难以理解，但实际上它们非常擅长转录带有口音的语音，它们理解说话者，但它们只是基于口音，对说话者存在一种隐性的等级观念。

items.title: 富钾盐替换普通盐有助于每年预防数百万人死亡
items.content_text: 澳大利亚乔治全球健康研究院的研究人员评估了在 193 个国家将食盐供应转换为富钾盐的健康益处。他们发现，全球每年可预防近 300 万例死亡和 1000 万例心血管疾病和肾脏疾病新发病例。富钾盐是通过用氯化钾替代部分氯化钠（即普通食盐的主要成分）制成的。它在外观、味道和烹饪方式上都与普通食盐一样。2025 年世界卫生组织（WHO）认可使用富钾盐来降低血压和心血管疾病风险。全球范围内，30-79 岁成年人中有三分之一患有高血压，相当于约 14 亿人。心血管疾病（CVD）是全球死亡和残疾的主要原因，2023 年导致 1920 万人死亡，过去 30 年增加了近 50%。虽然潜在益处很大，但一个担忧是晚期肾病患者出现高钾血症（血钾水平过高）的风险。然而，研究发现，即使在晚期肾病患者中，益处也大于风险。

items.title: Swift 天文台从印尼上空重返大气层
items.content_text: NASA Neil Gehrels Swift 天文台于 11 月 4 日 7:39 a.m. EST 从印尼苏门答腊上空再入大气层，坐标为北纬 3.4 度、东经 98.6 度。天文台的大部分组件在重返大气层过程中烧毁，可能有部分组件幸存下来。Swift 天文台重 1.5 吨，于 2004 年发射升空，旨在研究高能伽马射线暴的起源。过去 22 年受大气阻力的影响 Swift 天文台的轨道高度在缓慢下降，过去两年的太阳活动加速了其坠落。今年 7 月 NASA 曾尝试了一次拯救任务，但任务失败。

items.title: 任天堂最大 ROM 芯片供应商准备退出
items.content_text: 任天堂 Switch 游戏机实体游戏卡带使用的 ROM 芯片供应也受到了 AI 热的影响。任天堂最大 ROM 芯片供应商旺宏电子在其第三季度财报中宣布它准备终止 ROM 芯片生产，脱离游戏行业。旺宏电子表示，ROM 芯片的产量在过去一年中缩减了 39%，目前仅占其业务总量的 5%。ROM 芯片正逐渐被利润更高、需求更旺盛的其它存储芯片所取代。这意味着任天堂未来只能依靠其它 ROM 芯片供应商如罗姆（Rohm）和蓝碧半导体（Lapis Semiconductor），意味着游戏卡带生产成本可能会进一步上升。任天堂已经承诺未来会继续提供实体游戏卡带，不会效仿索尼只提供游戏的数字版本。

items.title: 新型牙刷通过产生电对抗牙菌斑病原体
items.content_text: 一款新型牙刷可通过刷毛移动产生电能，进而可对抗产生牙菌斑的病原体。在为期 3 个月、涉及 115 名志愿者的试验中，牙刷在减少口腔中导致龋齿和牙周炎的细菌方面的效果优于常规的机械刷牙法。牙刷是人类对抗牙菌斑的最强战士，它每晚都能物理性地清除牙齿上的细菌生物膜。然而细菌总会卷土重来，因此每天早晨都会重新开始这场战斗。北京大学口腔医学院的研究人员研发出一种牙刷，其压电单丝刷毛在刷牙过程中弯曲时会产生电荷。这一过程会产生活性氧，进而能破坏牙齿上的生物膜。在实验室中，该装置能有效杀灭口腔病原体，如牙龈卟啉单胞菌（Porphyromonas gingivalis，可引发牙周炎）。研究人员还在真实口腔环境中评估了这种牙刷的实用性。他们将这种牙刷分发给总计 115 名志愿者，这些人都接受了相同的刷牙指导。根据对样本的基因测序和宏基因组测序结果，志愿者口腔中有几种口腔病原体的相对丰度有所下降。总体而言，与传统尼龙刷毛牙刷相比，这种牙刷能更好地控制牙菌斑、减轻牙龈炎症和出血。

items.title: AMD 营收预计将首次超过英特尔
items.content_text: AMD 周二公布了 2026 财年第三季度财报，营收同比增长 45% 达到 134 亿美元。其中数据中心业务贡献了 85 亿美元营收同比增长 97%。客户端与游戏业务部门的营收下滑了 8% 降至 37 亿美元。作为 AMD 在 x86 市场的主要竞争对手，英特尔下一季度营收预计为 150-160 亿美元，其增长几乎停滞。相比下 AMD 预计下一季度营收将达到约 170 亿美元。如果达到这一目标，这将标志着 AMD 营收首次超过英特尔。

items.title: 韩国游戏 PC 启动器被植入恶意代码
items.content_text: 韩国游戏《胜利女神：新的希望（NIKKE）》的 PC 启动器被植入恶意代码。恶意代码是通过纂改 Level Infinite CDN 分发的四个官方 JavaScript 文件实现的，篡改发生于 2026 年 9 月 27 日前后，攻击则始于 2026 年 10 月 23 日到 11 月 3 日，在此期间打开 PC 启动器的用户可能会被植入木马。恶意程序会窃取浏览器保存的密码、Windows 凭据管理器信息、SSH 密钥以及云服务或 AI 服务的访问令牌，还能窃取 28 种基于浏览器的加密货币钱包数据、执行任意命令、读取文件以及屏幕截图。攻击期间打开过启动器的玩家可以打开游戏文件夹，搜寻 debug.log，打开该文件后寻找 k2f_chan，如果找到且显示 registered，那么最好立即卸载游戏并用杀毒软件进行扫描。

items.title: 法国银行被盗走 1.18 亿欧元
items.content_text: 法国国民互助信贷银行（Crédit Mutuel Arkéa）被黑客通过欺诈性交易盗走 1.18 亿欧元。被盗走的钱随后被转移到多个加密货币账号。该银行证实遭到网络攻击，但尚未证实 1.18 亿欧元的数字，只是表示攻击已得到控制，客户不会遭受任何经济损失。国民互助信贷银行暂停了其应用的部分转账功能。

items.title: Firefox 测试迷你窗口功能
items.content_text: Mozilla 正在新版 Firefox Nightly 中测试迷你窗口（Mini Window）功能。该功能类似视频画中画功能，将一个标签页作为独立窗口一直显示在当前标签页之上，这个窗口隐去了地址栏、各类控件、滚动条等常见标签页元素，但如果用户将鼠标悬停在迷你窗口内，各种标签页元素将会显示。迷你窗口方便用户在当前标签页上工作的同时参考迷你窗口的内容，免于在两个标签页之间反复切换。用户可以在专注于当前标签页的同时查看迷你窗口。

items.title: 富士胶片因 AI 热加大磁带产能
items.content_text: 富士胶片表示它将大幅增加磁带产能，原因是磁带备份成为 AI 热的一个意外受益者。普通消费者可能早在几十年前就已不再使用磁带，但业界却从未将其抛弃。云服务巨头依靠磁带对海量数据进行备份。富士胶片称，大型云服务商和数据中心运营商正在扩大对磁带的使用，因为磁带能以相对较低的成本存储海量数据。磁带备份可以轻松与系统断开连接，存放在抽屉、保险库或独立设施内。富士胶片强调，磁带介质能实现物理隔离（air-gap），为用户数据提供最后一道防线。

items.title: Nexus Mods 公布 AI 生成内容政策
items.content_text: 最大 PC 游戏 Mod 分享托管平台 Nexus Mods 公布了 AI 生成内容政策。Nexus Mods 没有禁止 AI 生成 Mod，但对此类 Mod 的分享设定了更严格的规定。新上传 Mod 必须披露是否使用 AI，AI 辅助 Mod 必须说明如何使用 AI 以及 AI 的使用范围。现有 Mod 需在 2027 年 1 月 2 日前符合新要求。如果 Mod 作者无视平台方提出的要求，可能会面临权限受限或被下架的后果。它计划针对 AI 使用、AI 模型训练、分支和衍生 Mod 引入新的授权选项，默认选项为“需征求作者同意（Ask me）”。Nexus Mods 承诺绝不会利用用户上传的 Mod 训练 AI，也不会将其出售或授权给任何 AI 公司。Nexus Mods 严禁利用生成式 AI 生成虚假的游戏截图。

items.title: 苹果开始在中国推出 Apple Intelligence
items.content_text: 苹果从 11 月 4 日起开始在中国推出 AI 功能 Apple Intelligence，中国用户可通过最新的 iOS 开发者 Beta 版进行测试，AI 功能将于 12 月随 iOS 27.3 的发布正式推出。中国版本的 Apple Intelligence 是苹果和阿里巴巴合作推出的，基于阿里巴巴的千问模型。首批 AI 功能包括实时翻译、写作工具、视觉智能、照片 app 的消除工具、智绘表情、照片 app 中的自然语言搜索、在照片 app 中创建回忆影片、识别优先邮件、邮件摘要、智能回复、通知摘要、首要通知、减少干扰、备忘录 app 中的音频转录摘要、通话转录文本的摘要、输⼊⽂字与 Siri 对话、Siri 能接入千问（需登录千问）、创作等。

items.title: 出生前后大脑会清理突变神经元
items.content_text: 根据发表在《自然》上的一项研究，出生前后大脑会清理突变神经元。对 2300 多个神经细胞进行的分析显示，在从人类胎儿大脑中采样的神经元中，超过 1/4 出现了染色体片段增加或缺失的情况。相比之下，出生后婴儿大脑中的神经元中，只有约 6% 存在此类异常。研究结果揭示了一种新的机制，该机制不仅调控着一个人的神经元数量，还决定了哪些胎儿神经元能够在大脑中存活下来。针对小鼠的研究表明，在早期发育过程中，哺乳动物会通过激活一个导致细胞死亡的分子程序，清除大量脑细胞。分析结果显示，在胎儿发育过程中，存在数量惊人的、具有广泛拷贝数变异的细胞。然而出生后，这些异常神经元的比例下降至原来的 1/4，表明它们在发育过程中已被淘汰。大脑是如何分辨哪些神经元正常、哪些不正常呢？一个可能的线索是那些拷贝数变异水平较高的脑细胞，其与其他神经元建立连接（即突触）的基因也往往表现异常。

items.title: SUSE 因 AI 而计划裁员十分之一
items.content_text: 德国开源软件公司 SUSE 现有员工 1900 人，它计划裁掉十分之一的员工。CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen 在电子邮件里表示，自动化和 AI 降低了某些岗位的需求。他表示做出这一决定是非常痛苦的，但也是必要的。Van Leeuwen 称，在被瑞典私募股权投资公司殷拓集团收购后，公司在仔细审视了其未来战略、所需能力及团队架构后做出了裁员决定,“显而易见自动化和 AI 正从根本上改变软件公司的运营方式。AI 技术正呈指数级发展，迫使我们彻底重新构想工作模式。无论是所在行业，还是在更广泛的经济领域，我们都已经看到了这一趋势。这意味着 SUSE 目前所依托的组织架构和成本基础，已无法支撑未来的成功发展。”受影响的员工将在 11 月 4 日前收到通知，员工代表将于次日选出，一对一沟通会议则将于下周初启动。

items.title: Bethesda 宣布《上古卷轴VI：哨兵》
items.content_text: 在 2018 年宣布《上古卷轴VI》八年之后，Bethesda 宣布了游戏的副标题《上古卷轴VI：哨兵》。知名游戏记者 Jason Schreier 称，该游戏至少还要两年时间才会面世。Bethesda 是在庆祝工作室诞生四十周年的视频中公布这一消息的。《上古卷轴VI》是与《星空》一同宣布的，2023 年 9 月《星空》发售后游戏才进入正式开发阶段，预计至少到 2028 年 Bethesda 才会公布更多游戏相关信息。

items.title: Chromebook 统治美国校园，AI 成了没得选的「套餐」

items.title: Dropping Out of the Electoral College
items.content_text:
The US midterm elections of 2026 have created a new opportunity. The "blue wave" has flipped enough state legislatures that it may be possible to complete the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact and make the Electoral College obsolete.

The NPVIC has a simple plan: all states in the Compact agree to commit their electoral votes to the winner of the popular vote nationwide. But to make it work, there need to be enough states in the Compact to reach 270 votes, the number needed to clinch a presidential election. Looking backward at presidential elections. this system would have had created different outcomes. (Here's a previous discussion on the Blue from 2014 when New York joined, but before the age of Trump). It would also push presidential candidates to shift their focus (and, of course, their money) to larger states, which would upset leaders of the swing states that typically get showered with that attention. The Compact would also need the approval of Congress, but not the President. However, there still aren't enough Democratic senators to overcome a filibuster and pass it.

items.title: Trump Admits He Ignored Court Order to Begin Building His Arch
items.content_text:
The Trump administration admitted Thursday that it has done work on the president’s planned 250-foot arch in Washington, D.C., in defiance of a court order.
In a court filing, DOJ lawyers acknowledged that a construction firm contracted by the White House, Grunley Construction Company, had painted lines in Memorial Circle, where President Trump wants his triumphal arch to be built. In their filing, they said that the company would stop its work and provide advance notice before resuming “any future work related to the project,” as they did not have permission from the National Park Service.
Meanwhile, the National Capital Planning Commission is expected to vote to approve the arch Thursday evening, and the administration wants to start work immediately after approval. Almost 1,000 pages of public comments have been submitted to the commission opposing the project, and three lawsuits have been filed to stop the arch from being built.
Veterans groups say the arch’s large size would hurt Arlington National Cemetery by casting a large shadow over it, which the Trump administration even acknowledges. However, it says the gargantuan monument should be built anyway.
Trump wants his arch badly, and he has openly expressed disdain for court orders against him in the past. After Republicans got a historic thumping in the midterm elections, it would not be surprising if Trump decides to blaze on ahead and try to build his arch quickly before the Democratic majority is sworn in and tries to stop him.

items.title: Massie Says He Has Enough Signatures to Force Vote on Epstein Files
items.content_text:
Republican Representative Thomas Massie says he has enough support to force a vote on his second Epstein Transparency Act.

“When we return next week, we’ll get 218 signatures for Epstein Files Transparency Act II, which guarantees a vote,” Massie wrote Thursday on X. “Survivors will be able to get their own records, State Attorneys General can prosecute crimes, and we can take the DOJ to court for keeping critical files hidden.”

Massie, who has made an enemy of Trump by opposing the Iran war and pushing for the full release of the Epstein files, first passed the Epstein Transparency Act in November 2025. And though President Trump signed it into law, Massie, Democrats, and a few Republicans argue that his administration didn’t fully abide with what the act required.

“The Department of Justice has flagrantly and consistently ignored EFTA’s disclosure requirements,” Massie wrote earlier this summer in his announcement of the Epstein Files Transparency Act II, co-sponsored by Democratic Senators Ben Ray Luján and Jeff Merkley, and Democratic Representatives Ro Khanna and Teresa Leger Fernández.

“The Department of Justice continues to unlawfully withhold over 3 million Epstein files that should be released to the public,” he continued. “In addition, the DOJ is unlawfully maintaining heavy redactions on the files it is releasing. State attorneys general and victims should have the right to sue the Attorney General of the United States to compel compliance with a transparency law President Trump signed.”

items.title: Jamie Raskin Warns Law Firms That Caved to Trump to Watch Out
items.content_text:
House Democrats are coming for law firms that cut deals with President Donald Trump.

Speaking on MS NOW Wednesday night, Representative Jamie Raskin, who is poised to become chair of the House Judiciary Committee, said that the several law firms that struck deals with Trump could expect to receive subpoenas next year.

In the early days of Trump’s second term, the president issued several executive orders revoking the security clearance of and threatening to pull all federal contracts from large law firms that had supported clients and causes he felt were contrary to his agenda. In response, nine firms agreed to degrading deals that gutted their work on certain policy areas such as immigration, ended company DEI programs, and required them to provide pro bono legal work for Trump’s administration. Altogether, the deals signed with the president amounted to nearly $1 billion worth of free legal work.

“There are major law firms in America, including Paul Weiss, that have capitulated to these coercive tactics from Donald Trump and have basically surrendered and made all sorts of outrageous concessions,” Raskin said on MS NOW.

Trump’s executive order had targeted Paul Weiss over the work of Mark Pomerantz, a former prosecutor who previously oversaw the Manhattan district attorney’s office’s investigation into Trump’s alleged financial crimes. As part of bowing to Trump’s threat, the firm acknowledged that Pomerantz had committed wrongdoing, and agreed to stop making decisions about hiring and promotions based on considerations of diversity, equity, and inclusion.

The current ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee, Raskin had requested information from several firms about the exact details of their agreements; the answers they provided indicated that the president may have gotten the short end of the stick. While the firms had reportedly agreed to provide millions of dollars of pro bono work for specific causes, many asserted that they had total authority over the selection of their clients.

A group of Democratic lawmakers sent another series of letters to law firms earlier this year, warning that the Trump administration’s scheme to use “coercive and illegal measures” to blackmail firms could potentially violate federal laws against bribery, defrauding the public, and even racketeering.

items.title: North Carolina Senate Race Was Over Before Election Day Even Began
items.content_text:
Roy Cooper won North Carolina’s Senate seat before the polls even opened on Election Day.

The number of early votes cast for the Democratic nominee totaled more than 1,728,000, besting the total number of votes cast overall for his Republican opponent, Michael Whatley, by roughly 85,000 votes, according to the North Carolina State Board of Elections. By the time the polls closed, Whatley received 1,643,000 votes, while Cooper received nearly 2,468,000 in total.

Cooper managed to flip the seat blue, helping the national caucus obtain a majority in the upper chamber. He will replace outbound North Carolina Senator Thom Tillis, who announced his retirement earlier this year.

Speaking to a crowd at his victory party in Raleigh on Tuesday, Cooper pledged to orient his focus in Washington toward affordability and ending the war in Iran.

“I am still a prisoner of hope,” Cooper said. “I truly believe that our best days lie ahead, that we can make the course correction that our great country so badly needs. That North Carolina and the United States have a future teeming with possibilities.”

Cooper previously served as the Tar Heel State’s governor from 2017 to 2025, but his election on Tuesday was just one component of a blue wave that swept over the historic battleground state.

Despite a gerrymandered map that was intended to give Republicans a steep advantage on Tuesday, Democrats gained at least five House seats and are projected to win a sixth. Five districts in the state have yet to report their final vote counts, but so far, Republicans have won zero seats. (Current forecasts estimate they will win four.)

items.title: Democrats Are This Close to Being Able to Override a Trump Veto
items.content_text:
The Democratic Party has amassed such a strong majority in this week’s midterm elections that they may be able to challenge President Donald Trump’s veto power.

Republicans’ only remaining hope to thwart Democratic majorities’ plans rests in Trump’s veto power. However, the president’s veto can be overridden by a two-thirds majority congressional vote, equivalent to 290 votes in the House and 67 votes in the Senate.

Democrats are projected to win at least 250 seats in the House of Representatives, and are reportedly on track to win roughly 260 seats total, meaning that they will only need to convince 30 Republican lawmakers in order to bypass the president’s official objections. Twenty-nine House races remained undecided Thursday.

As the results rolled in Tuesday night, and a Democratic majority appeared imminent in both chambers of Congress, Trump posted an image of a red MAGA-style hat that read “VETO.” Now, it seems that the president can’t even count on that as the Democrats continue to defeat his party members.

items.title: Democrat Who Dropped Out Still Beat Republican in Deep Trump Country
items.content_text:
Democrats apparently didn’t even need to run to win over Trump country this midterm election.

Iowans were so pissed off with Republicans on Tuesday that they elected Eric Armstrong to the state House. The catch: Armstrong, a retired railroad executive, pulled out of the race in September due to health issues.

Nonetheless, he bested his Republican opponent, Keith Jones, by roughly nine percentage points, or 865 votes, according to results tabulated by the Associated Press.

On September 7, Armstrong posted to his Facebook account that he would step away from the race effective immediately.

“Running a successful campaign requires immense physical and mental energy. Recently, I have been facing some personal health issues that require my full attention and immediate care,” he wrote at the time.

“Because I must prioritize my health and recovery at this time, I am stepping down from my campaign, effective immediately,” he continued. “This was a deeply difficult choice. However, I know it is the right one.”

Armstrong was still elected to fill a state House position vacated by Josh Turek, who managed to flip Iowa’s U.S. Senate seat on Tuesday.

It’s an enormous change of pace from how Iowa’s 20th House of Representatives district was feeling even two years ago, when it swung in favor of Donald Trump by a margin of 20 percentage points. Beyond that, Iowa’s politics have been about as Trumpian as it gets: The state voted to send the MAGA leader to the White House all three times he was on the ballot.

Speaking with The New York Times via phone Wednesday, Armstrong said he would “do my best to represent” Iowa’s 20th district.

“But I still have health issues, that’s what I’m struggling with,” he noted.

Even if he has to miss votes, local political experts argue it won’t be a huge cause for concern.

“Iowa has a part-time legislature that meets from January to May or so,” University of Iowa professor and expert on Hawkeye State politics Timothy Hagle told Newsweek. “If he had to miss some time it probably won’t be a major concern given that Turek missed a lot of votes this year,” given the priorities of Turek’s Senate campaign.

items.title: Hegseth Expands National Guard in D.C. Amid Arrest Over “Finger Gun”
items.content_text:
Amid reports that he may be on his way out, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has decided to expand the National Guard’s presence in Washington, D.C.

Politico, citing an October 29 memo, reports that Hegseth has authorized the National Guard to begin using Humvees, light medium tactical vehicles, several dozen marked police cars, and boats in the district—though there isn’t a clear reason why.

Soldiers with the National Guard still aren’t allowed to pursue suspects or make arrests, and the vehicles Hegseth is allowing were used in the Afghanistan and Iraq wars. The memo states that the boats will be conducting “perimeter security” for police targeting suspected gang leaders and drug traffickers in Anacostia, the southeastern corner of the city, but won’t be surveilling U.S. citizens. Federal officers “must always be on board” the boats “to help arrest a criminal suspect,” according to the memo.

On Wednesday, D.C. police charged a man with “threats in a menacing manner” and assault on a police officer for allegedly pretending to shoot at National Guard troops by making a “finger gun” gesture. Those kinds of headlines are what make the National Guard’s presence in the city unpopular, and beefing up their vehicles will only make them further seem like an occupying army to D.C. residents.

While the memo was drafted before the finger-gun charges and Republicans’ historic defeat in the midterm elections, this kind of move would seem to be a direct challenge to the new Democratic-controlled Congress, as well as Washington’s Mayor-elect Janeese Lewis George, who is on record as opposing the deployment of the National Guard in the district. This move could hasten an impeachment vote against Hegseth and set up a showdown between George, backed by Congress, and President Trump.

items.title: Newsom Moves to Save Everyone on California’s Death Row in Final Act
items.content_text:
Democratic California Governor Gavin Newsom commuted the sentences of 548 death row inmates in one of his last acts in office. This is the largest death sentence commutation in American history.

“I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us,” he wrote in an open letter Thursday. “I know we cannot execute people in our imperfect legal system and remain true to our core values, first among them justice and human decency.”

Those on death row will instead serve life without parole. The California Supreme Court must now review the commutations of death row inmates with multiple felony convictions,, a process that has no clear timeline.

California has more inmates waiting to be executed on death row than any other state, representing one-quarter of death row inmates in the entire country. Newsom’s office noted that of the 548 people on death row, 220 have waited 15 years or more for legal representation to fight their cases. The last person to be put to death in California was 76-year-old Clarence Ray Allen in 2006.

This move also comes as Newsom decides whether or not to run for president in two years.

“This will always weigh heavily on me. As Governor, I alone bear the responsibility for this decision and its impact, just as I alone would bear responsibility for each execution,” Newsom concluded. “For this reason, I am compelled to follow my conscience and, as authorized by our Constitution, take this action for the welfare of the state of California.”

This story has been updated.

items.title: Calls to Replace Jeffries and Schumer Explode After Democratic Wins
items.content_text:
Calls for Representative Hakeem Jeffries and Senator Chuck Schumer to step down from their leadership positions are growing as the dust from Tuesday’s midterm election settles. The calls—coming from inside and outside of Congress—cite a lack of vision, an unwillingness to go after Trump, the continued acceptance of corporate PAC money, and an extreme deference to the Israeli government. 

There are lots of questions circulating about Schumer’s future in Senate leadership. Minnesota Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan declared on election night that it’s “time for new leadership” in the Senate. Senators-elect James Talarico and Abdul El-Sayed have also expressed doubt in Schumer’s future as leader, with El-Sayed even introducing Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen as the “next Senate majority leader” earlier this summer. Van Hollen himself said on Wednesday that “no one should be committing to anybody as the next Democratic leader” without having a conversation around a bold agenda. “It’s not a time for incrementalism. It’s a time to move forward a very bold kitchen table agenda.”

Jeffries hasn’t escaped without criticism, either. A Change.org petition to replace Jeffries and have an open election for House speaker has reached over 500,000 signatures. House Democrats start with a party vote to select a speaker before that candidate is confirmed by the larger House in January. 

“Hakeem Jeffries currently serves as House Democratic Leader and has previously been nominated by House Democrats for Speaker. If his name is put forward again, House members will have a choice to make. Hakeem Jeffries is simply not the right choice,” the petition, which was shared by actor Mark Ruffalo, reads. “We believe the Speaker should represent the Democratic voters, not just the Democratic establishment.” 

Nicole Whitted, the petition’s creator and a Change.org ambassador who receives compensation for the petition, explained her opposition to Newsweek.* “After historic wins on Tuesday, I believe the Democratic Party and our country as a whole is at a crossroads. My opposition to Hakeem Jeffries is about more than any single policy disagreement,” she said. “Hakeem Jeffries has longstanding political and financial ties to corporate interests and influential pro-Israel lobbying organizations. He also held a private meeting with Jared Kushner, President Trump’s son-in-law and outside advisor, who himself is being investigated by the Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee. These relationships and decisions raise serious questions for me and many of those who have signed this petition about transparency, political influence, and whose interests Democratic leadership is ultimately serving.”

Opposition to Jeffries’s potential speakership grew even louder after his strangely conciliatory comments on Wednesday regarding whether the Democratic Party will retaliate against the Trump administration’s corruption and violence now that it has a staunch majority. 

“The American people don’t want us to get even, they want us to get things done on their behalf,” Jeffries told MS NOW, specifically ruling out impeachment as a top priority. “We ran on affordability, we won on affordability, and now it’s our job to govern on affordability.”

Hakeem Jeffries on Morning Joe: The American people don't want us to get even. They want us to get things done on their behalf because life is way too expensive.

We ran on affordability, we won on affordability, and now it's our job to govern on affordability. pic.twitter.com/b5ieQUbMRO

— Clipping Wings (@ClippingWings) November 4, 2026

That notion was met with quite a bit of backlash. 

“I don’t know who needs to hear this, but you can focus on affordability issues—and— hold criminals accountable,” Campaign for New York Health executive director Melanie D’Arrigo wrote. “When you don’t hold criminals accountable, you’re giving them a strategy to be more successful next time.”

“This isn’t even about revenge or politics, it’s about the reality that if there aren’t consequences & prison time for quite a few people, all the worst parts of the last decade will keep happening,” writer Kylie Chueng added. “He fundamentally misunderstands the moment & can’t be speaker.” 

“Let’s be clear here: conducting meaningful oversight to expose waste, fraud, abuse and corruption isn’t about getting even, it’s about being watchful stewards of taxpayer dollars,” Texas Democratic Party adviser Kurt Bardella wrote. “It’s the job.”

“They fired all the black and gay people, cut cancer research, cut healthcare for millions, cut food for starving children, killed hundreds of schoolgirls, separated families, put kids in camps, and shot people in the street,” a large liberal account wrote. “We better get fucking even.”

Newly elected democratic socialist Representative Chris Rabb of Pennsylvania has already declined to endorse Jeffries’s speakership, saying that he needed to address issues like Medicare for All first—which Jeffries currently opposes.

Jeffries was also criticized for his deep ties to Israel. Jeffries is one of the strongest Democratic supporters of Israel, and one of AIPAC’s top recipients, as the majority of Democratic voters oppose more aid to Israel in the wake of its genocide of Palestinians. A clip of Jeffries declaring, “Israel today, Israel tomorrow, Israel forever!” at a 2014 rally—a paraphrasing of infamous racist former Alabama Governor George Wallace’s 1963 demands for segregation—has also begun to recirculate. 

Hakeem "America is back" Jeffries, who is set to become Speaker of the House, said at a 2014 rally:

"Israel today, Israel tomorrow, Israel forever!" pic.twitter.com/aud5JeBMxu

— HatsOff (@HatsOffff) November 4, 2026

To make matters worse, after the election, AIPAC praised the Democrats who would remain by Israel’s side, mentioning Schumer and Jeffries by name and promising to keep funding candidates of either party as long as they continued to support Israel.

“AIPAC congratulates the hundreds of pro-Israel Democrats and Republicans who won their elections last night,” the controversial lobbying group wrote on Wednesday. “We congratulate Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer and House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries on the resounding victories for their caucuses.… Our community will increase its support for Democrats and Republicans who recognize that a strong partnership with Israel helps keep both countries secure, advances peace and stability, promotes democratic values, and grows our economy through trade and innovation.” 

“Bye,” newly elected California Representative and Democratic Socialists of America member Angela Gonzales-Torres replied.  

* This story has been updated to reflect the compensation of the Change.Org petition creator.

items.title: “That’s a Problem”: Fox News Crashes Out Over Democrats’ Wins
items.content_text:
Across the board, Fox News hosts are struggling to cope after the midterm elections dealt a catastrophic blow to the Republican agenda they’ve spent months hyping up.

Speaking on The Five Wednesday, host Jesse Watters spiraled out about the many groups of voters that had evidently defected from supporting Republican candidates.

“The coalition has totally collapsed. You lost whites. Whites!” Watters cried. “You can’t do that if you’re a Republican. Men! Hispanics, big-time! And so it’s gonna take a while to put the coalition back together because it’s in the heartland.”

Co-host Greg Gutfeld tried to spin the disaster for Republicans, suggesting that it would be “fun, fun, fun” to watch Democrats struggle to fix all of the problems Republicans had created.

“I think you’re missing the bigger picture, is that the American people, young, men, white, Americans, said screw you Donald Trump, said screw you to the Republican Party in places in the deep South, in the Midwest. And that’s not just something that happens all of the time, that’s a problem that the Republicans have,” Watters said.

Speaking on his own show later that night, Fox News’s Sean Hannity ranted bitterly about Hasan Piker, the left-wing political commentator.

“Now before, nobody in the Democratic Party stood up to Hasan Piker, and that wing of the party, but the inclusion party, they did kick out Haley Stevens. She’s out of the party. That’s what we’re dealing with,” Hannity said.

Hannity blamed Piker for Democratic lawmakers who urged Republicans to “LAWYER UP” ahead of a flood of congressional investigations. “Now, perhaps they were taking inspiration from the Democratic Party’s spiritual leader Hasan Piker who wrote, quote, ‘We’re gonna put your ass in jail, everyone get more woke right now.’”

He then urged Republicans to “stay away from finger pointing or blame.” I guess for Hannity, that only applies when the problems are caused by Trump.

items.title: Top Justice Department Official Resigns as Rats Begin Jumping
items.content_text:
Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon is leaving the Trump administration.

Fox News reports that Dhillon resigned Thursday following Democrats’ landslide victory in the midterm elections. She reportedly told allies that she planned to leave after the elections, according to Bloomberg Law.

Dhillon is the first top official to leave the Trump administration following the election. She overhauled her division at the DOJ to actually weaken civil rights, and on diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives, said, “Either DEI will end on its own or we will kill it.” She also staffed the civil rights office with the worst lawyers, including people with criminal records, misconduct allegations, a love of conspiracy theories, and a history of hacking election sites. Dhillon also led a sweeping campaign to force states to turn over sensitive voter information, a crusade repeatedly shut down in court.

In September, Dhillon proudly announced that the DOJ had dropped more than 50 desegregation cases, most of which were in Southern states with Jim Crow histories. On her watch, the office focuses on everything but civil rights, looking at election rolls, immigration, and alleged antisemitism on college campuses.

Dhillon’s departure could be the first sign of people fleeing a highly unpopular, lame-duck administration. Others could be fired, such as Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, whom Trump has been considering giving the axe. White House adviser and deputy chief of staff for policy Stephen Miller has plenty of enemies upset that his hard-line immigration policies made Republicans massively unpopular.

items.title: Trump Is Losing Power. Marco Rubio’s Next Move Proves It.
items.content_text:
The MAGA movement’s Tuesday bloodbath has already inspired some of the far-right contingent’s biggest figureheads to plot a course without Donald Trump.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio is preparing to resign from the Trump administration as he lays the groundwork for a potential 2028 presidential campaign, The Independent reported Thursday.

Insiders in Washington and the British government told the newspaper that Rubio needs to distance himself from Trump’s controversies—including the wildly unpopular war in Iran—to improve his odds at the ballot box.

The news would be a major snub to Vice President JD Vance, who has been teasing his own presidential bid for months and has long been viewed as Trump’s only clear successor.

Both the White House and the State Department refuted reports of Rubio’s forthcoming exit, telling the Independent that the allegations were “baseless.” But the possible Republican challenge may not have come as a surprise to Trump himself, who speculated to reporters Wednesday that “maybe [Vance] won’t run.”

“We’ll see what happens. Everybody—You don’t know who’s talking about running. You could have a lot of people, maybe a lot of people running, maybe nobody is gonna run. Maybe he won’t run. I don’t know who’s going to run,” Trump said, before adding that he “wouldn’t have done nothing different” regarding the Iran war.

If Rubio does decide to leave, he will leave behind a shattered and broken White House that is on the cusp of losing even more Cabinet members as Trump looks for places to lay blame for his shoddy second term.

Last month, Trump reportedly called several close confidantes to assess the potential of using White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, his former campaign manager and famed “Ice Maiden,” as a scapegoat for a major midterm bust. He’s also made the rounds to check current attitudes about Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman General Dan Caine as the Iran war drags on into its eighth month.

But even more heads could roll after January, when Democrats retake both chambers of Congress. Liberal party leaders indicated Thursday that they plan to make Washington a very different place in the new year. Some Republicans seem to be in agreement: Representative Thomas Massie plans to resurrect his articles of impeachment against Hegseth, and several members of the GOP believe it will pass.

items.title: Pete Hegseth May Get Impeached Before Dems Even Take Over Congress
items.content_text:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth doesn’t need a blue wave to knock him out of office—Republicans are already pissed enough on their own. 

Outgoing Representative Thomas Massie told CNN Wednesday that he plans to trigger a vote to impeach Hegseth when Congress returns next week. Multiple GOP sources said they expect the measure to pass. 

Massie introduced his impeachment articles in mid-September as a privileged resolution, requiring the House to vote on it within two days. House Speaker Mike Johnson called an early campaign-season recess in order to kill the measure, but Massie told a reporter that he’d take up the effort after the midterm elections. 

Following previous reporting that Donald Trump intended to oust Hegseth as the fall guy for the Republicans disastrous midterm elections, the president told ABC News Thursday that he had “every intention to keep him.”

Massie had his own response. “If Trump’s going to replace appointees like Hegseth, he should do it while he can still get the replacements confirmed in the Senate,” he wrote on X Thursday.  “Also, my Hegseth impeachment resolution is a much gentler version of what’s coming when Dem’s control Congress. They’ll have hearings & trials.”

The previous evening, Massie had warned, “There is one contingency in which I won’t reintroduce the articles of impeachment: Hegseth resigns.” 

While House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has suggested that Democrats are not interested in “getting even” with Republicans, he indicated Thursday that the Defense secretary would be a potential target when he became House Speaker.
